BIOGRAPHY OF THE PRIEST STUDENT Zhu An Si1

NOTE 1

His real name is Chu Mong Nhan, also known as Tu Nhan, nickname An Si, and is an intellectual in Con Son land.

He understood the Sutra Pitaka and believed deeply in the Pure Land dharma, so he took the title Hoai Tay Layman. He often considered that all sentient beings commit countless karmas, of which more than half are due to the two karmas of adultery and killing, so he immediately composed two books to advise people to abandon adultery and killing.

The book advising people to abandon killing is called Van Thien Tien Tu,2 the words are passionate and sincere, the profound meaning touches people's hearts. According to his story, every time he passes by any temple, he makes a prayer:

“Praying to all the gods, please develop your mind to ascend to this world, do not enjoy offerings made from the flesh and blood of sentient beings, and wholeheartedly recite Amitābha Buddha, praying for rebirth. This Western Pure Land, from the age of 24 until the end of his life, vowed that if he personally killed even a small fish, or anyone in my family, if anyone harmed a mosquito or an ant, I would ask God to severely punish me, and thunder and lightning would destroy the books I wrote. While saving and releasing animals, you still have the intention of killing, you will also be subject to the same punishment as above.

About the book advising people to give up their lust, the title is The Sea of ​​Desire Returns to Crazy,1 advises all those who are heavy in lust, to first use the means of contemplating the prison-like state of being in the mother's womb, clearly see all the sufferings, and thus immediately get rid of the mind of lust.

NINE THINGS IN BUDDHA'S REMEMBER

VICTORY

1. The Buddha's name has only a few words and is very easy to recite, unlike sutras and mantras which are difficult to recite.

2. You can recite Buddha's name anywhere, not necessarily in front of the Buddha altar.

3. You can recite Buddha's name at any time, regardless of morning or evening, when busy or idle.

4. Anyone can recite Buddha's name, regardless of the rich or the poor, the wise or the foolish.

5. People who recite Buddha's name will have their merit increase.

6. Those who recite Buddha's name will be eliminated from serious sins. In the sutras, it is taught that: "Reciting the Buddha's name with one mind can destroy eighty billions of kalpas of serious sins in life and death."

7. People who recite Buddha's name are respected by gods and goddesses.

8. People who recite Buddha's name must stay away from evil demons.

9. When a person recites the Buddha's name, when they are about to die, they will definitely receive a prediction from the Buddha.

SOME CONCEPTS IN DAO

BUDDHA ON Reincarnation

1. The heavens in the three realms

- Desire Realm: 6 heavens

- Form Realm: 18 heavens, including:

- First Jhana: 3 heavens

- Second Jhana: 3 heavens heaven

- Third jhāna: 3 heavens

(A total of 28 heavens in the three realms.)

2. Four ways of birth (four births)

Includes beings born from eggs (ovum birth), from fetuses (fetal birth), from moisture (low birth) and from transformation (biochemistry).

3. Six realms of samsara (six paths)

1. The heaven of the gods.

2. The human realm of humanity.

3. Asura realm.

4. Hell.

5. Realm of hungry ghosts.

6. Animal realm.

There are a number of different ways to distinguish these 6 realms. Like when talking about 2 good paths, it refers to the 2 realms of heaven and human, but when talking about 3 good paths, it also includes the asura realm.

Similarly, when talking about 3 evil paths, it refers to the realms of hell, hungry ghosts and animals, but when talking about 4 evil paths, it also includes the asura realm.

Thus, only the asura realm can be considered as good realm (good path) or evil realm (evil path).

Answer: There are two classes of Bodhisattvas. Firstly, Bodhisattvas who have practiced for a long time, have been close to Buddhas, and have attained the Dharma of Non-birth tolerance. Second, Bodhisattvas have just recently awakened their minds, have never been close to Buddhas, and have not yet attained the Dharma of Non-birth.

Bodhisattvas who have practiced for a long time must have great supernatural powers, so they can transform into gods, kings, ghosts, or animals, enter and exit life and death, and help sentient beings. If a person is new to practice and has weak and fragile strength, although he has developed the Bodhi mind but is still in the ordinary world and cannot save himself from his own suffering, how can he save others?

Therefore, Dai Tri Do's treatise teaches: "If it is said that ordinary people are still full of hindrances, have great compassion, and wish to be born into the impure world to save suffering sentient beings, it really does not make sense. Why is that? Because in this world with the five impurities, things such as sound, form, money, fame and fortune... every moment and every moment are constantly pulling and binding, and those with hatred and afflictions are always densely surrounding, just a little bit. If you accidentally fall into the path of falling, even if you are born as a human being, it is difficult to meet the Buddha when you are born. If you are lucky enough to believe in the Buddha, become a monk and become a monk in the next life, you will not be able to avoid being infatuated with worldly conditions and create many evil karmas.

Therefore, if a person has wisdom, if they want to save sentient beings, they must first pray for themselves to be met

Buddha. If you can recite the Buddha's name with one mind without confusion, you will definitely be reborn. At that time, you will have an indestructible diamond body and will be able to practice your wish to save all kinds of sentient beings. Just like if you want to save a drowning person in the middle of a river, you must have a boat to rely on, then you can save the person from the water. If there is no support and recklessly jump in to save someone, it will be inevitable that we will drown together.

Therefore, it is not a lack of compassion, but skillful use of that compassion.

Second Doubt

Question: The essence of all dharmas is emptiness, never having been born before, always equal and passing away, why do you leave this place and seek that place, wanting to be born in the Western Pure Land? In the sutras it is taught that: "If the mind is pure, the Buddha land is pure." If you want to pray for a pure world, you must first purify your mind. Why don't you pray for a pure mind but instead pray to be born in the Pure Land?

Answer: People who want to be born in the Western Pure Land, if it is said to leave this place to seek that place, then the person who does not seek to be born in the Western Pure Land, can it be that they are not leaving that place to seek this place? If you say that whether you are here or there, you will not seek rebirth, that is falling into attachment, thinking that after death it is all over. If we say that we don't let go of this place or that place, then that is falling into the attachment to permanence, thinking that everything will last forever.

The Vimalakirti Sutra teaches: "Even though we know that Buddha lands and sentient beings are all empty, we still practice to purify the land and educate all sentient beings." Therefore, even though you have a strong desire to seek rebirth, it is not contrary to the principle of non-birth.

Even the teachings "pure mind, pure Buddha land", must also be understood in terms of both appearance and nature. If we consider the nature of reason, why do we think that people who seek birth in the Pure Land have an impure mind, while people who do not seek birth in the Pure Land have a pure mind? In terms of appearances, if you can keep your mind pure in the midst of an evil world with five impurities, how can you keep your mind as pure in the world of Ultimate Bliss? What's more, in the case of people in this impure world, although they seek purity, their minds are not pure, compared to people born in the Pure Land, although they do not seek purity, their minds are still naturally pure?

Third Dogma

Question: In the Buddha lands throughout the ten directions, merit is equal. Why not think extensively about all the merits and pray for birth in all the pure Buddha lands, but only pray for birth in the pure land of Amitābha Buddha?

Answer: The pure lands of all Buddhas are of course equal. The only thing is, the majority of sentient beings are stupid and impure, and if they don't concentrate in one place, it will be difficult to achieve concentration. Therefore, concentrating on reciting Amitābha Buddha's name is the method of concentrating the mind towards a single object.

The Sutra on Vows for Rebirth says: "Bodhisattva Universally Extensive asked the Buddha: 'In the ten directions there are pure Buddha lands. Why is the World-Honored One so inclined to praise Amitābha Buddha's Western Pure Land and instruct those who seek rebirth there?'

“Buddha taught Bodhisattva Universally Extensive: ‘The sentient beings in Jambudvipa have their impure and chaotic minds, so I am inclined to proclaim only one pure Buddha land in the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, to help sentient beings concentrate on a single realm to easily be reborn.’”

The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches: “All Buddha bodies are the same. is a Buddha body. Just like a bright full moon, reflecting in all places with water.”

So know that reciting one Buddha means reciting all Buddhas, rebirth in one Pure Land is no different from rebirth in all Pure Lands.

Fourth Doubt

Question: The Buddha lands in the ten directions are limitless and boundless, depending on the thought of any Buddha, he can be reborn [in that Buddha's land], why only recite Amitābha Buddha?

Answer: There are three relationships. First, Amitābha Buddha and this Saha world already have a predestined relationship. From countless previous lives, he made forty-eight great vows, all because he wanted to lead sentient beings to recite

Buddha to his pure land. Nowadays, people in this Saha world who open their mouths to recite Buddha's name are reciting Amitabha's name. [In the sutras it is taught that] sentient beings in the future have a fragile merit, when the Dharma is about to disappear, all the sutras will be lost, only the Amitabha Sutra remains for another hundred years, isn't that also proof of this karma?

Second, as taught by Buddha Shakyamuni. In the three collections of twelve sutras, the Buddha's teachings are extremely extensive, only regarding the method of reciting the Buddha's name and reciting the name, the Buddha did not teach reciting any other Buddha but only reciting Amitābha Buddha. If this is not an absolutely essential thing, why did the Buddha have to insist on it many times?

Third, because the Buddhas of the ten directions all demonstrated their conviction. Because the Pure Land method is extremely difficult to believe and accept, when the World-Honored One preached about Amitābha Buddha, Tathagata Buddhas from ten directions appeared together to prove that it was true, making it impossible for those who witnessed it to believe.

Therefore, if one practices pure karma, is there any reason not to focus on reciting Amitābha Buddha?

Fifth Doubt

Question: Ordinary people are full of hindrances, heavy evil karma, all afflictions have not been ended, not even an iota of merit has been cultivated, and

like the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss is transcends the three realms, surpasses even the heavenly emperors, and the gods are hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of times greater than the Ganges. An ordinary person like that recites Buddha's name, how can he be born in that Buddha land?

Answer: That is thanks to the power of Amitābha Buddha, not based on that person's own power. For example, if a person has a missing leg, even if he limps all day, he will not be able to travel many miles, but if he can ride on the precious elephant of the Holy King of Chakravarti, in one day he can travel through all four worlds. Just like a poor student who wants to be close to the king, if he participates in small competitions from different continents and districts and hopes to pass the exam to become an official and gain a noble and glorious position, it is indeed very difficult and still uncertain. If one can be born as a king's son, then in no more than ten months one can live in the same house with the king. People who can be reborn only rely on the Buddha's power, it's the same.

If a practitioner does not develop the mind to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, and only tries to practice in this evil, dirty and impure world, he will have to endure drifting and sinking. He does not know how many lifetimes he has to go through but still cannot become an Arhat, let alone reach the Bodhisattva status.

If you practice according to the Pure Land method, you just need to diligently practice and achieve undisturbed single-mindedness, then you can be reborn in this life. That person will continue to practice in the Western Pure Land, forever without turning back or falling, straight to Buddhahood, which is indeed the shortest path.

For example, if an insect lies in a bamboo tree, if it wants to escape and move towards the top, it must cut through countless bamboo segments, with unbearable hardship and difficulty. If you know how to rotate horizontally and carve your way out, it will be very easy and quick. That's why Pure Land practitioners are said to take a shortcut out of the three realms. How can there be any doubt that ordinary people [reciting the Buddha's name] cannot be born in the Pure Land?

Sixth Doubt

Question: Among the nine levels of rebirth, the three lower levels belong to the lower level1 and most of them are evil people who only believe in reciting the Buddha's name when they die and can be reborn. For example, what if they have been born in the Pure Land but still have wrong views, greed, anger, and delusion?

The nine rebirth levels include the three highest levels: the upper level of upper birth, the upper level of middle birth, and the top level of lower birth; The three grades at the average level are upper middle grade, middle grade middle grade, middle grade lower grade; and the three lowest levels are the upper lower level, the middle lower level and the lower lower level.

Answer: I'm just afraid of not being able to be reborn, and I don't worry about the fact that once I've been reborn, I'll return to being evil. In this matter there are five causes and conditions. First, receive the blessings from the great compassionate vow of Amitābha Buddha. Second, in that realm, all wishes are fulfilled, so there is no need to give rise to greed. Third, the precious trees, birds, and flowers in that world all preach the wonderful Dharma. Fourth, surrounded by only Bodhisattvas as good friends. Fifth, long lifespan, can go through many lifetimes of practice.

Therefore, once reborn in the West

Ultra Bliss, you can go straight to Buddhahood, there will be no turning back forever, you can be sure of that.

Seventh Dogma

Question: Following Buddha Shakyamuni, Bodhisattva Maitreya will become Buddha, and is currently preaching in the Tushita heaven. Those who can practice the ten good karma of the highest rank will definitely be born in that heaven. Why not pray to be born there, to be close to Maitreya, in the future when he is born as a Buddha, he will follow him to this world?

Answer: Cultivating ten good karma to be of the highest quality, of course you can be born in heaven, but if you want to decide to be born in the Tushita heaven, I'm afraid it's not certain. Haven't you read the Maitreya Sutra? That sutra teaches: "Practice the samadhi dharma, enter deep into right concentration, only then can you be born [in the Tushita heaven]." Let's ask, is that what people who practice ten good karmas are like?

As for Amitābha Buddha, just by reciting his name, no one cannot be guided, compared to people who generously practice ten good karmas, it is many times easier.

Furthermore, in the Tusita heaven there are mostly deities who have abdicated their positions in the Desire Realm. There are so many celestial women there that it is impossible to count them. Many of the gods who have seen them are often infected, let alone mortals?

The Ni-gang-tu Sutra says: "The greatest bondage of the gods is nothing more than female form. Women bind the gods and lead them into the three evil paths." If compared to the Western realm of Ultimate Bliss, it is incomparable.

What's more, if you meet Bodhisattva Maitreya but have not yet attained sainthood, how can you be reborn in the pure realm once and never turn back [like rebirth in Ultimate Bliss]?

The Eighth Doubt

Question: Ordinary people from many past lives up to now have widely created countless evil karma. When they die, they only recite Buddha's name ten times, how can they be reborn?

Answer: People who commit evil karma in this life But when he was about to die, he could return to his mind and recite the Buddha's name for ten times and be reborn. That must have been practiced in many previous lives. However, in this life, he was temporarily born confused and followed an evil path.

If that were not the case, then when he was about to die, evil and evil conditions would definitely have to be found. How could he instead meet a wise man who taught him how to recite the Buddha's name? Moreover, even if one is taught to recite the Buddha's name, how can one hear it and immediately believe and receive it?

What's more, at the time that person recites the Buddha's name at the end of his life, he must have regained enlightenment in his heart, sincerely repent of his previous mistakes, in his heart he must be extremely afraid of evil deeds and earnestly pray for rebirth, so he wants

destiny suddenly let go, there was only one path left towards the Western Pure Land, there was absolutely no other place to turn. Reciting Buddha's name like at that time, just one sentence is equivalent to thousands of words. That's why the Sixteen Contemplation Sutras say: "In every single thought, eighty millions of lives of sins in life and death can be eliminated."

If one can understand that diligence and sincerity, and also have the blessings and good karma from previous lives, then there is nothing to doubt about being guided by the Buddha?

The Ninth Doubt

Question: The Pure Land is ten thousand million Buddha lands far from this Saha world. So far away, how could ordinary people be born there at once? Have you heard that women, people lacking the senses and the Second Vehicle cannot be reborn? Can that be believed?

Answer: The distance is difficult to reach, talking about physical appearance. A thought that can come immediately is about consciousness. People reciting Buddha's birth to the Pure Land are only saying that this mind is born, not bringing their physical form to that realm. For example, if a person dreams of going to another country, even though it is thousands of miles away, he wakes up as soon as he wakes up. Is it possible that because the road is near it is easy to wake up but the distance is difficult to wake up?

To say that women with people with defective roots are not born in that world, that is to say that in the world of Ultimate Bliss there are no women, no people with defective roots, does not mean that women with people with defective roots cannot be reborn. about Ultimate Bliss.

If it is said that women cannot be reborn, why did the World-Honored One predict that Mrs. Vi-de-hy and her 500 maids would definitely be reborn? The Infinite Life Sutra contains 48 great vows of Buddha Amitabha, one of which is: "After I become Buddha, all women in countless worlds, if they hear my name [immediately rejoice and believe, develop Bodhi mind,] will be disgusted with the female body. After death, they will no longer be reborn as a female."1

NOTE 1

This is the 32nd great vow.

For women, this is the case, so for people with impaired intelligence, it can be inferred and known. Furthermore, like starlings and parrots, they can also be reborn by reciting Buddha's name.2 So, is it possible that people with defective roots are not as good as animals? Those who come to the Second Vehicle are all those who have attained fruition. Ordinary people can still be reborn, so is there any reason to exclude people of the Second Vehicle? The Amitabha Sutra teaches: "Amitābha Buddha has boundless and limitless Shravaka disciples, all of whom are Arhats." So how can it be said that there is no Second Vehicle? Therefore, that statement means that the person born in the Pure Land no longer carries the attachments of the Second Vehicle, so it is said that the Second Vehicle is not born. Just like saying that the Second Vehicle cannot be reborn in the Pure Land, that is completely unreasonable.

The Tenth Doubt

Question: Now I have decided to develop the wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, but I do not know what deeds to practice, what wishes to generate to be reborn in the Pure Land? Furthermore, all worldly people have wives and children, and have not stopped lusting after lust. I don't know if that will enable them to be reborn or not?

Answer: People who decide to seek rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, in addition to reciting the Buddha's name, if they have two other strong thoughts, will certainly be reborn. The first is a mind of disenchantment with the impure world. The second is the mind of admiration and love for the world of Ultimate Bliss.

You should also develop the mind of Bodhi, depending on your ability, do good deeds, dedicating them to rebirth in the Pure Land. With that being said, there will never be anyone who cannot be reborn.

It's not a hindrance to having a wife and children in a secular place. We just need to be able to make our wife and children benefit from the Dharma, know how to practice, and stop cultivating evil causes.

Regarding being tired of leaving the impure world, that is to say, in this impure life, every move and every move is a pit of thorns and pits that can easily fall into depravity. People in this world are miserable for the rest of their lives just because of the two words, food and clothing, chasing after two paths of fame and fortune, running around all their lives, busy with their hands and feet endlessly, resigned to being servants to their wives and children, hundreds of thoughts, thousands of dreams at night, all of which are searching for this body and shape to bring trouble.

Imagine for yourself, this body about seven meters tall1, its external appearance is only thanks to the thin layer of skin covering it, and it is falsely claimed to be of great nobility. If you could use the heavenly eye to take a look, you would see that the inside is filled with a dirty belly, with dirty blood, pus, and phlegm. Therefore, the Nirvana Sutra teaches: "This body is like a city, the residence of foolish rakshasa demons." So, is there any wise person who would love to indulge in this body without getting bored of it?

NOTE 1

Each ancient ruler is about 33 centimeters, seven meters is equivalent to about 2.1 meters.

Regarding admiration and love for the world of Ultimate Bliss, that is to say, the joy in the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss, even though the heavenly palace cannot compare, cannot be imagined and described in language. Every day, just remember to think of the words in the sutra, calm your mind and consider each word, thinking that in the future you will definitely be born in that place, then naturally thoughts of admiration will arise, and the cause and effect of the Pure Land will also mature.

What is the development of Bodhi mind? The Commentary on Rebirth says: "The Bodhi mind is the vow to become a Buddha. The vow to become a Buddha is to have compassion for all sentient beings in the six paths of samsara, who are suffering from endless suffering, so we develop the mind of salvation, wanting to help all be able to escape the three realms, to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, and only then will we fulfill our vow."

If a person reciting Buddha's name has the above two strong thoughts, in addition to having developed the mind of Bodhi, respectfully relying on the Tathagata's wish for salvation, if he cannot be reborn or receive the Buddha's prediction, that is unprecedented.

Doubts about Pure Land practice1

Question: About the profoundness and simplicity of the Pure Land dharma, it has now been explained. But those who achieved enlightenment in Zen Buddhism said that "seeing the nature and becoming a Buddha", so why do we need to go back and pray for rebirth?

Answer: That is only talking about those who achieved enlightenment, for

so those who vow to be reborn are all because they have not yet achieved enlightenment. But if you are enlightened, you will be able to quickly head towards the Pure Land, even if ten thousand buffaloes are not strong enough to hold you back.

And as in China. In the United States, there is Vien Cong in Lo Son, the elders of the Thien Thai, Hien Thu, 1 sects, everyone praises and encourages the practice of Pure Land, praying for rebirth in Ultimate Bliss. Question: The Pure Land Dharma teaches us all the fundamentals, it is truly profound and far-reaching. However, that world called the Pure Land is hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha lands away. Compared to the theory "right here in the mind is the Pure Land, the true nature is Amitabha" does it seem to contradict each other?

Answer: The Shurangama Sutra teaches that: "From outside this physical body to all mountains and rivers, space, earth... are all objects located in the true mind. clear color.” It is also taught that: "All dharmas are born because of the mind appearing."

So, is there a Buddha realm outside the mind? You should know that outside the mind there is no realm of water, outside of the realm of water there is no mind. Therefore, it is said that the countless lands in the ten directions, as numerous as the number of small dust particles, are all just lands in our mind; The Buddhas of the three generations are as numerous as the grains of sand in the Ganges River. They are all just Buddhas in our minds.

If we understand this, there is no world that is not established in our mind, and there is not a Buddha that is not manifested in our true nature.

So then, the world of Ultimate Bliss, which is hundreds of millions of millions of Buddha lands away, is it a separate world that is not created by the mind? Amitābha Buddha in that Pure Land, is it possible that he is only a Buddha without manifesting our true nature?

Question: The Pure Land theory is all about external appearances. A wise person should go straight to Zen Buddhism to achieve enlightenment, that is more lucid. If we only know how to praise Pure Land practice, isn't it that we are attached to appearance and do not clearly know the nature?

Answer: According to the origin, the nature is not two, but the means of getting there must be divided into many paths

paths. Understanding this meaning, you will see that between Zen Buddhism and Pure Land, although the paths are different, they still return to the same source.

Master Trung Phong taught: "Those who practice Zen, are the meditation methods of the Pure Land; those who practice Pure Land, are the Pure Land methods of Zen."

Even though we support and promote each other like that, practitioners must choose one subject to penetrate. Therefore, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva who attained Samadhi of Buddha's Recitation said that using the mind of Buddha's name can enter the Ring of Non-birth. Bodhisattva Samantabhadra entered the realm of inconceivable liberation in the Avatamsaka Sutra and said: "May when I die, I will be reborn in the Pure Land." Those two great Bodhisattvas, one next to Śākyamuni Buddha, one next to Amitābha Buddha, each of them should have taught their own Dharma, but they were all in perfect harmony and did not hinder each other. How can it be said that they still have prejudices?

Furthermore, as you said that the Pure Land is a method of external appearance, doesn't that mean that the pure mind is the Pure Land, and there is no Pure Land adorned with the seven treasures? If that is so, then you can also say that the good mind is heaven, after all there are no heavens like Da-ma, Dao-loi...; that the evil mind is hell, after all there is no hell like mountains of knives, forests of swords, pots of boiling water...; that the foolish mind is an animal, after all there are no animals with fur and horns?

However, there is a pure land in the quiet illumination [of the true mind], there must also be [corresponding] dignified realms of true retribution that can be known. What's more, apart from facts there is no reason, apart from appearance there is no nature. If we insist on abandoning things to seek truth, leaving appearances to find nature, surely reason and things cannot be unobstructed, how can we expect to reach the realm of "unobstructed things" [as in the Avatamsaka Sutra]?

Furthermore, although he already has the Tathagata nature, he still has an ordinary human body. If you really can reach the Pure Land anywhere and everywhere, is it possible to fall into a toilet and still be considered lying on a bed? Can dogs, pigs, buffaloes, and horses eat together at the same trough? Is it possible to sleep together in the same bed with a rotting corpse and crawling maggots? If you can do so, you will be able to accept what he said, that "high mountains and flat lands, everywhere is the Western Pure Land", that "even in the midst of mountains of swords and forests of swords, there is always peace and freedom". If that is not the case, then in the place of seeing impurity is not yet empty, the feelings of love and hate are still there, overestimating one's view, boasting and boasting, easily causing people with shallow views, who only read a few scriptures, learn martial arts to draw a few Zen koans, [after hearing it immediately] want to slander the Dharma, creating a cruel crime, so whose fault is that?

Question: The person Practicing to escape birth and death, therefore attaches great importance to the principle of non-birth. Admiring the Western Pure Land

if you make a vow to be reborn, can that be considered relying on the meaning of non-birth?

Answer: Seeing birth and thinking it is birth, that is the mistake of the eternal view, thinking that everything is permanent. Seeing that there is no birth and thinking that there is no birth, that is the confusion of the view of annihilation, thinking that everything is gone. Being born without being born, not being born but being born, that is the truest and ultimate meaning. The mysterious true nature is inherently unborn, but due to the harmony of causes and conditions, form arises. Because the essence has the ability to take form, it is said that non-birth means birth; Because form is manifested by nature, it is said that birth is non-birth. Understanding this, we know that being born in the Pure Land is just the birthplace of the mind. If you suspect that because it is far away, it is difficult to reach, then [you should know] that the mind covers the whole of space, embraces the entire dharma world, how can there be anything far and near?

Question: The Buddha land in the ten directions is pure, with many miracles, now why does it only refer to the world of Ultimate Bliss, singling out that realm's sublime scene, sublime fate?

Answer: This world is the convergence of all suffering. For example, if there is some cause for pleasure, it will inevitably lead to suffering. The Pure Land is not like that, so the Sutras teach that: "The sentient beings in the Pure Land have no suffering, they only enjoy pure pleasure, so it is called Ultimate Bliss."

Now let's briefly compare a few things between the two realms, to see the difference between heaven and earth.

In this world, sentient beings must immediately spend ten months in the mother's womb, and at the time of birth, life and death in an instant. In this world, when people reach old age, their skin becomes wrinkled and their hair turns gray, their knees become tired, their backs become hunched, they have to be lifted and guided when standing or sitting, and their breathing is weak. In the Pure Land, thanks to the dharma that nourishes the spirit, it will never weaken or get old. All the lands in the ten directions can come and go at will in the blink of an eye. Thus, the suffering of old age and frailty in human life is no more.

In this world, once sick, one groans on the hospital bed, rolling around and wailing. In the Pure Land, there are great magical powers and great power. Throughout the land, there is never any sound of sickness or discomfort heard. Thus, the suffering and illness of human life are no more.

In the Pure Land, once reborn in the lotus flower, you will immediately have an indestructible diamond body, excellent light, and an infinite lifespan. Therefore, these blind people cannot know the exact shape of an elephant for the rest of their lives.

For example, before that, don't let them touch the elephant with their hands. Surely, just a few words of description can help them know what the elephant looks like, without causing any dispute. Just because once they have their own simulation,

those people all think that they have accurately experienced it with their own hands, there is absolutely no need to doubt anymore, and immediately consolidate that knowledge into a solid prejudice in their mind, which cannot be erased.

Therefore, people who do not read Confucian books, if they hear the Pure Land dharma taught, will not accept it even if they do not believe it. go to the extent of defamation. But once he has read more or less Confucian books, he immediately thinks that it is the most accurate truth, relying on his limited knowledge to boast, thinking that the Pure Land dharma is just the teachings of Buddhism alone, [not comparable to the Confucian saints and sages]. That's why sincere words are seen as myths, precious nectar is seen as poisonous wine.

That's why it is said that the obstacle of reason [obstinacy] is heavier than lust.

tieu_de: First, you must believe that there are three generations
noi_dung:
First you must believe in three lives

There are people who study according to Confucian books, because they do not believe in past and next lives, so they do not believe in the Pure Land theory. I really don't know that the past life and the next life are just like yesterday and tomorrow, they are all inherently inherent, not created by the Buddha. Just like the internal organs: heart, liver, kidneys, lungs... are all available in the patient's body, how could it be possible that because those things were described by the doctor, they would assume that they must be objects in their medicine basket?

Wenchang Dejun just opened the poem "The Sound of Nature Van" and said: "I have spent 17 generations as a powerful scholar." According to that statement, it is clear that there is a previous life and a next life. Everyone who follows the path of academics and career must go under your supervision. Is that not enough to believe and accept your words?

tieu_de: Then you must deeply believe in cause and effect
noi_dung:
After all, one must deeply believe in cause and effect

If Confucian students do not believe in cause and effect, it is not because they do not believe in Buddha's teachings, but rather because they do not believe in Confucian doctrine.

The I Ching [of Confucianism] says: “The person who does good deeds must have abundant joy, Evil deeds will bring many disasters." The Book [of Confucianism] also says: "Those who do good deeds are bestowed with hundreds of good things. Those who do evil deeds are bestowed with hundreds of disasters."

Accordingly, doing good or doing evil is the sowing of causes, encountering good deeds or disasters, is reaping the results, [just a different expression between Confucianism and Buddhism.] Just like calling it "sun" or "sun", they all refer to the same thing.

So [in Buddhism] it is said: "If you want to know the causes of previous lives, look at the results of this life." If people believe in the theory of cause and effect like that, they naturally don't dare to do evil things. They think that retribution is just a myth, so they like to lie and deceive others, without fear of anything.

For example, in a village, there is a person who believes in humanity

and should do a good deed; Ten thousand people who believe in this will add ten thousand good deeds. On the contrary, there is a person who does not believe in cause and effect and does an evil deed; Ten thousand people who do not believe like that will increase ten thousand evil things.

That's why it is said: "Everyone believes in cause and effect, that is the path of great prosperity for society; everyone does not believe in cause and effect, that is the path of great chaos for society."

tieu_de: Confucius definitely talked about the theory of three generations
noi_dung:
Confucius must have talked about
about the theory of three generations

About the theory of three generations,1 researched in the scriptures and history books and found many records, but according to what people know today, they are not the same.

NOTE 1

The theory of three lives: that is, the belief that there is a present life, a past life, and a future life that will be reborn after death.

People who study Confucianism, just because they think that Confucius never talked about that theory, they themselves do not mention it. However, is it true that Confucius did not say that theory?

If it is said that Confucius did not know the theory of three generations, then he is not really worthy of being considered a saint. In a set of Analects [there are twelve thousand seven hundred words,] the words spoken by Confucius himself are only eight thousand five hundred and three words. Thus, there must be a lot of things Confucius said that were not recorded and passed on to future generations.

If we wait to see the records in [Confucian] scriptures before believing, it must be that in the Four Books and Five Classics, Confucius never mentioned his parents, then Confucian students also avoid mentioning their parents; Confucius never talked about his brothers, so Confucian students also avoid talking about their brothers; Confucius never talked about his house and land, so Confucian students also avoid living in houses and developing their careers.

Not only that, but the four necessities of writing are paper, pen, ink and ink stone, Confucius never mentioned it, so practicing writing today is wrong. Furthermore, in addition to thin summer shirts and winter fleece shirts, Confucius never mentioned other types of clothing, so it must be assumed that wearing pants today is wrong. In addition, like the staff made in Jiangnan, the Confucian dynasty should not use it, and the pigments made in Western Shu, the Confucian dynasty should not be used for painting. Why is that? Because Confucius never mentioned those things in Confucian scriptures.

Now, considering only what is taught in Confucian scriptures, such as Confucius teaching people to respect parents and be harmonious with brothers and sisters, Confucians do not follow it; Confucius taught people to be honest and tolerant, but Confucians are not honest and tolerant. Confucius never taught people to gamble, but Confucians now love gambling games. Toan sees things like Confucius never taught to do this and that... then the Confucianists follow and do things like this and that... what does that mean? To put it briefly, it is [learning without] thinking.

tieu_de: Wise people should not accept that life is short
noi_dung:
A wise person should not take for granted that life is short

Humans consider that in the beginning there was no death. The word "death" only exists in this flesh body. But although our physical body has changed, our true nature has never changed.

For example, when people go far, sometimes they row a boat, sometimes they sit in a palanquin, sometimes they ride a horse, sometimes they drive a car... [vehicles change in all kinds, but the person never changes]. Boats, palanquins, horses, chariots... those are the physical body, and the person rowing the boat, sitting in the palanquin, riding the horse, driving the car, that is the true nature.

If we consider the physical body, it is not more than a hundred years long, but if we consider our original appearance, it is not only as long as heaven and earth [but much more]. Thinking carefully about it, there really is nothing more enjoyable.

People today do not believe in an afterlife, that is, they only know the physical body without knowing the true nature. This is clearly assuming that one's life span is short, which is also a wrong point of view.

tieu_de: Wise people should not close their views
noi_dung:
Wise people should not close their views
views

In the awareness of poor farmers, they often do not know the activities of rich people; in the perception of the rich, but unaware of the life of the king. Even though they are in the same human world, the classes of high and low, high and low, are very different from each other, let alone compare humans with the gods of heaven, or compare heaven with the Pure Land of Buddhas.

People think that those who read a lot of books must have a wide range of knowledge. But I don't know that [there are cases] the more I read books, the narrower my understanding becomes. That is because of stubbornness in the knowledge that has been received before, cementing in the heart a prejudice that cannot be erased or changed.

In general, people's place of seeing and knowing is only within the scope of a country, not knowing that the number of worlds is endless, the number of suns and moons is also endless. Short-sighted people only know that humans were originally born in the Pangu Dynasty, but do not know that from the first eon the world was just established, from the time the Great Equality King opened the country onwards, up to now the ninth small kalpa has gone through; I only know this one country, called China, but I don't know that in this one continent Jambudvipa, the place I call myself China, there are actually sixteen great countries, five hundred

medium-ranked countries and ten thousand small countries; Only knowing that humans can live to the age of seventy is considered "rare in the past", not knowing that from their earliest lives humans have lived an average of eighty-four thousand years before dying; I only know that in this place, if you want clothes, food and drink, you have to work hard to plow the fields and weave cloth, not knowing that in the heavens or Pure Lands of the Buddhas, just thinking about those needs will naturally appear; I only know that it is extremely difficult to obtain gold, silver, and money in this world. I do not know that in the Buddha lands of the ten directions, the ground is made of seven treasures; only knowing that the writing in this world was created by the Six Books1 method of Cangjie, not knowing that since the founding of the world, there have been sixty-four ways of writing; Only knowing a few books such as Ta Truyen, Quoc Ngu, Historical Records, Chinese Books... quickly assumed he was a noble person of scholarly literature, not knowing that on the Pho Quang Minh Palace, chests containing books were piled as high as mountains;We only know that the human body, flesh and bones are formed by the harmony of the father's sperm and mother's blood. We do not know that the physical body is deposited into the lotus fetus and is born in the fragrant realm of the utmost purity, completely not coming from the mother's womb; I only know that when I marry a skinny and pale wife, I will love and pamper you very much, cherish you like gold like jade, and enjoy listening day and night to the sound of golden chirps; Little did they know that when King Chakravart was on the throne, besides the Jade Lady

NOTE 1

Six books: Six principles of writing writing, including: pictograms, indications, meanings, sounds, turns and imitations. Chinese writing (Chinese characters) is formed according to these six principles.

is the main wife, there are also up to twenty thousand beautiful ladies following her, even like the Heavenly King in the Dao-loi heaven, the number of pearl ladies alone is up to tens of thousands of billions; Next to each of these jade girls, a body of the Heavenly King appeared to enjoy the pleasure; We only know that humans are the most spiritual species among all species, and can help us to be brought into the civilization and nourishment of heaven and earth. We do not know that humans are just one of the six paths of reincarnation, one of the four ways of birth, and one of the ten dharma realms; Only knowing how to worship a few saints, they consider them to be incomparable, in addition to all other saints, they insist that they are not worth believing in, insist that what they have never seen are myths, not knowing that each country has a number of saints presiding over the education, humanity has many countries, in the world of Jambudvipa there are a total of six thousand four hundred different races, not just in the new country of China. There are saints!

Alas! Such vast realms, how can those who only know how to run after sound, form, money and material gain a glimpse of it? For example, an earthworm only knows the joy of eating soil within a meter range, but does not know the green dragon leaping in the middle of the ocean, struggling in countless waves. Like a beetle, it only knows the joy of hiding in a pile of dirt, but does not know the eagle flapping its wings to fly ninety thousand miles away, riding the wind and the clouds.

Therefore, people who study Buddhism need to have a very clear view.

tieu_de: The Buddhist scriptures are a must-read
noi_dung:
Buddhist scriptures must be read
through

Chickens, dogs, buffaloes, goats... can only cry out loud but cannot speak. If compared to humans who can speak, the ability to speak is truly precious. Illiterate people, who can only speak but cannot write, compared to people who have learned a few words and can write letters to communicate with people far away, then those who have learned those few words are already very valuable. People who learn those few words, although they can write them down to replace words, cannot write words that express the thoughts and feelings of hundreds of thousands of people, nor can they retain what they have written until hundreds of thousands of years later. If one can learn a lot, understand the stories of the past, and write them into books to leave behind for future generations. Surely just one book can be printed into hundreds of thousands of books, one book can be saved for hundreds of thousands of years to come. Wouldn't a person like that be even more precious?

However, those are just worldly books. If, in addition to the books of Confucianism, we can expand our reading through the Buddha's Sutras, then everything in heaven and earth, past lives and after lives, up to [the books in] the deep sea treasures of the Dragon Palace, can all be known through a general outline, so wouldn't the understanding be very profound?

But even if the understanding is profound, if we cannot find a direct shortcut to escape the three realms, Surely there is still no part for the Bodhi seed.

If one can widely understand the Sutra Pitaka, encounter the Pure Land Dharma and wholeheartedly believe in it, respectfully practice it, then one's wisdom and merit will definitely not only be accumulated in five or three lifetimes but much more.

Some people raised the question: "Although the writings in the deep sea treasure in the Dragon Palace are related to the true teachings of the Tathagata, why do Confucian students not believe them to be true?" Answered: "The stories about King Yao, King Shun, King Vu of the Xia Dynasty, King Thang of the Shang Dynasty, and even King Wen and Vu of the Zhou Dynasty, if told to illiterate people, they would all consider them to be myths." Therefore, regarding the Buddhist scriptures, it is absolutely impossible not to read them.

tieu_de: Mr. Huyen Trang aroused and strengthened faith
noi_dung:
The Venerable Huyen Trang aroused and strengthened
strengthened faith

People in the world saw that there were monks who did not keep the precepts, so they felt contempt and did not believe in the Pure Land method. That's so wrong. This is like seeing a Taoist's poor character and then looking down on Lao Tzu; Seeing that Confucianism was corrupt, they looked down on Confucius.

Wise people should not rely on their

human status to evaluate and refute their words, let alone rely on the poor character of those who follow them to despise the Dharma?

Once upon a time, King Thai Tong once said to Dharma Master Huyen Trang: “I have an idea. I want to offer offerings to monks, but I heard that many monks are not virtuous enough, so what should I do?

Mr. Huyen Trang replied: "The land of Con Son has precious gems, also hidden in the mud and sand; Le Thuy district1 has gold, is it possible that there are no tiles, bricks, or gravel there? Clay or wood are used to create Arhat statues, if you develop a respectful mind, you will definitely be blessed; bronze and tin are cast into Buddha statues, and those who destroy them are definitely guilty. Dragons molded from clay cannot make rain, but if you want to pray for rain, you must pray for rain. use that earth dragon. Even though ordinary monks cannot give blessings, if you want to ask for blessings, you must know how to respect them."

NOTE 1

Le Thuy: A district in Zhejiang province, China.

King Tang Thai Tong was frightened when he heard those words and said: "From now on, even if I meet a little novice monk, I will pay the same respect as Buddha."

Praiseworthy, King Thai Tong of course already had blessings in his previous life, so he immediately woke up after just teaching once, but Mr. Huyen Trang was also truly a true master, skillfully arousing and strengthening people's faith.

tieu_de: You should develop a mind that is tired of leaving this physical body
noi_dung:
One should develop a mind that is tired of leaving this physical body

People live in a world tormented by eight sufferings, but do not know that they are suffering, on the contrary, they think it is pleasure, as if from a place of suffering, they will sink deeper into suffering, with no time to escape forever.

Let's talk about the suffering that arises, for example. The fetus lives in the mother's womb, below the liver, chest, above the large intestine, as a membrane filled with water, then gradually forms like a closed bag, unable to move freely. When the mother eats hot food, the fetus feels like being bathed in boiling water; When the mother drinks cold water, the fetus feels like it is lying on ice.

The place in the mother's womb is inherently unclean, and the food nourished through the mother's blood is also not pure. The time spent in the womb is no more than three hundred days, but the suffering experienced is equivalent to decades.

From conception to just one month old, one must endure the pain of reversing the body, with the head turned down towards the mother's body. The form gradually grows [until the days are full, at which point] it wants to escape but cannot. This is when the fetus is most at risk of death, and is also when the mother is in the most danger. When the midwife used her hands to pull it out, the fetus felt pain as if its body was being torn into many pieces.1 Therefore, any child who was just born cried loudly.

NOTE 1

The original work used 車裂 (xay), which refers to a cruel punishment in the past, using 5 chariots to pull the 5 at the same time. direction to tear the sinner's body to pieces.

When he was born, he had to lie in dirty, smelly excrement, never knowing shame. Even if they come from rich and noble families, they are the same; Even great saints and sages are like that. People just take things for granted because they are used to such things, so they never know. If we could quietly reflect on it in the dead of night, wouldn't we feel pitiful and shameful?

The Great Saint Tathagata, out of compassion for the world, teaches people who seek rebirth in the Pure Land and are reincarnated from lotus flowers to escape these sufferings. Why are we still immersed in the delusion of the worldly world, and not fed up with the body?

tieu_de: The filial son does not want to enter the womb
noi_dung:
The filial son does not want to enter
pregnancy

When the consciousness enters the fetus, not only does he himself suffer a lot, but the mother also has to endure countless sufferings. Not to mention ten months of pregnancy, every day feels as long as a year, and when it comes time to give birth, the mother also has to endure all kinds of pain, shame, and embarrassment that are hard to describe. Every second and every minute is close to death, every thought only wishes for survival. If you are lucky enough to overcome the difficulties of giving birth, you will love your child like a treasure. That's why the mother always lies on the wet side, the baby rolls on the dry side, raising and carrying her until she reaches adulthood, her life's essence and blood silently draining away.

Once upon a time, there was a novice monk who, when he was seven years old, asked his mother

ordained to study Buddhism. [Diligence in practice, at the age of 8] attained enlightenment, seeing and knowing the things of previous lives. When he saw what happened in his previous life, he immediately lamented: "Just this one body of mine has made five mothers suffer! In the first life, when I was born, someone in the neighbor's house also gave birth to a child. I died early, and my mother saw the neighbor's child grow up and was sad and miserable. In the second life, not long after I was born, I died. My mother, every time she saw someone else breastfeeding her child, remembered me and was extremely sad. In the third life, I was ten years old and died. Every time my mother saw children of the same age eating and drinking, she thought of me and was extremely sad. In her fourth life, I was not old enough to get married and died. Every time my mother saw people my age getting married, she remembered me and felt sad. Now in my fifth life, I have just turned seven years old and have become a monk. At home I miss her, and I also think about the world of birth and death, which is so confusing, causing suffering to my loved ones like that need to diligently practice the Right Path.”

Nowadays, on the path of life, people are crowded together, coming back and forth endlessly, most of them are those who cause suffering to their parents, and how many people can repay their parents' deep gratitude?

Once born in life is once to cause suffering to parents. Giving birth to hundreds or thousands of generations means causing suffering to hundreds or thousands of parents. If one can transcend the world and be reincarnated from the lotus [Place of Ultimate Bliss], then one will forever no longer cause suffering to one's parents

, then wouldn't that be a great filial person in the great filial piety?

Today, those who slander the Buddha Dharma, on the contrary, think that monastics are unfilial. Those people are willing to continue with the pregnancy, causing endless suffering for their parents.

tieu_de: Noble people should be ashamed of themselves
noi_dung:
Noble people should be ashamed of themselves

People worthy of being called noble are not due to high positions, great titles or extensive knowledge, but are those who have the ability to eliminate lowliness, who can eliminate the baseness and baseness, which makes people become like animals.

What is that baseness? Those are the greed, lust, killing, stealing, which make people become like animals. In addition to these things, the most embarrassing thing is that everything you put in your stomach turns into dirty, stinky excrement. Even if it's a precious dish with hundreds of flavors, once it's swallowed, it turns into a sticky mess that's no different from phlegm. When swallowed deep into the stomach, there are yellow parasites waiting there to devour day and night. After a day and night, the digestive process is completed, and when it is brought to the large intestine, it has a foul smell that no one wants to come near. Once the stomach is full, it must be released through the defecation. When it shoots out, the stench is no different from pig or dog feces.

such cowardice, like being caught once is extremely embarrassing, how can one endure it every day like that? If every day is like that without self-awareness, without developing a mind of boredom, then you are no different from a stupid animal.

Therefore, a person who knows how to think must use this to stop self-hatred, every second and every minute wants to eliminate those vile and lowly things, only then is he worthy of being called a noble and great person.

The gods in the six heavens,1 enjoy the delicious taste of heavenly nectar, fragrant, pure, clean and gentle, without a trace of dirt, so their bodies ride on the clouds. scent, appearing everywhere at will, in hundreds of thousands of realms of water can suddenly come and go, every day does not produce impure substances such as phlegm, feces, urine... Therefore, just a little fingernail or toenail of the gods is as valuable as this Jambudvipa realm. However, he is still not worthy of being called a great noble person, because he still has not escaped reincarnation.

NOTE 1

Here there are only six heavens belonging to the world of Desire (Desire Realm).

Therefore, one must definitely transcend the world, be reincarnated from the lotus flower in Ultimate Bliss, then only then can the above-mentioned vile things be forever eliminated. Within the scope of Confucius's teachings, it is absolutely impossible to help us reach such a point. [If you want to be liberated, you must only believe, accept and follow the Dharma of the Tathagata.]

For example, a silkworm makes a cocoon

The silkworm makes a cocoon, spins the silk to the left, right, then pulls it to the top, bottom, whatever is inside must be pulled out to form a cocoon, thinking that thanks to that, it can stay inside the cocoon, there is nothing to worry about. Who knew that his efforts to arrange himself like that were to tie himself up? Who knew that the method it relied on, which was to spit out all its silk to protect itself, would make people want to use the silk threads it released for profit, bringing disaster to its life? Thousands and tens of thousands of silkworms like that, not one of them escaped the disaster of being put into boiling water. Yet, this method of spinning silk to make cocoons is still passed down from generation to generation, causing them to continue to fall into boiling water. There is nothing more tragic!

People in this world have two doors closed to form a family cocoon inside. Exerting all his strength to do business throughout his life, insisting that he only knew how to earn money and clothes for his wife and children, plotting lies and deceit, taking revenge here and there, there was nothing he wouldn't do. By the time the inheritance is formed, you yourself are tied up in it, there is no way to escape.

Thousands and tens of thousands of ignorant people in the world are all like that, can anyone escape the retribution of the next day? However, such practices are still passed down from generation to generation, continuing to create bad causes, making it inevitable that no one will have to suffer the consequences of compensation. It is so strange that nothing else could be more strange!

Therefore, the Forty-Two Chapters of the Sutra teaches: "Human beings are bound by family, wife, children, and home, more than prison. Prison also has its miracles." The term was released, but as for his wife and children, there was absolutely no thought of separation, [how could he escape?]”

Example of a fishing net

Rural people in river areas often place fishing nets in flowing water to catch fish. Along the water's edge, there are places with thick green grass that can be hidden. They discreetly place them underneath the grass, so the fish can't get out after going in. The fish find a suitable place and scramble to get in, thinking they can hide and stay there, but unexpectedly they have crawled into the trap.

The traps [inheritance] in the river of desire are the same. People only know that in normal times, when there is no illness or trouble, a family can safely hide, a wife and children can be cared for, so they have a lazy and distracted mind, not worrying or thinking, not knowing anything. One day, the King of Hell suddenly appeared and pulled him out of the water. At that time, all relationships between husband and wife, father and child, mother and child... suddenly collapsed, and everyone could be caught by the hand of impermanence. When I think about it, I can't help but feel resentment, but resentment is just useless. The only way to avoid being caught is to be the wisest.

Horse example

Horses have four classes. The best and wisest horses just see the shadow of the whip and start running without waiting to be spurred. The next rank only needs one whip and runs away. In the third category, if you can't run with light whipping, you have to wait until you hit heavily before starting to run. The most stupid and incompetent horses will refuse to walk even if they whip them hard. They have to wait until someone uses an awl to pierce their skin, causing extreme pain, then they will take off their hooves.

Humans are similar in comparison. People with wisdom are easily alert. Hearing news of someone dying within a hundred miles around me, I was immediately frightened and thought: "Within a hundred miles around me, someone has died. I am also human, I must die too." Thinking like that, he quickly practiced and prayed for liberation. Just like that, we only see the shadow of the whip running.

The next type of people, when they hear that a relative in their clan has died somewhere, immediately wakes up and takes care of their practice.

The next type of person must wait to see a neighbor next door die before they wake up and [think about practicing].

If they wait until they themselves are old, weak, or sick to become enlightened and practice, then that is the type of horse who waits for the ax to pierce his flesh painfully before running.

If when you are old or weak, or sick, you still refuse to be mindful and practice, wouldn't you be worse than all the people mentioned above?

Example of a weasel

There is a wild weasel that sneaks into a person's kitchen at night, eats its fill, then falls asleep. When morning comes, it can't run away anymore, so it pretends to be dead and waits for someone to take it away.

Not long after, someone saw that the ferret was dead and wanted to throw it away. Suddenly someone said: "The tail is so beautiful, wait until I cut off its tail and then throw it away." The weasel was very scared when he heard that, but he had to try to endure the person cutting off his tail, still lying still as if he was dead.

Suddenly, a boy came, wanting to cut off his ears. The weasel was even more scared, but thinking to himself that even if he lost his ears, it wouldn't be enough to lose his life, he tried to endure it.

Not long after, he heard someone say: "This weasel's skin can be used to patch sheep's clothes."

At this point, the weasel was extremely frightened, thinking to himself: "If you want to skin me, you will have to cut off my head, cut open my stomach, how can I bear it?" Immediately got up and ran outside, finally escaping.

Humans live in the prison of the three realms, are they any different from [the weasel in] that kitchen? Due to the force of karma, one must be born as a human, it is difficult to avoid death. Only by relying on the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth, can we find a way out of that death.

If we let our strong youth pass [without worrying about practicing], we are no different from that weasel waiting to have its tail cut off. If you wait until you reach the grave when you are old, that means lying still and allowing someone to cut off your head and cut you open.

If you do not make a broad and deep vow, courageously forget yourself and practice, how can you escape the path of delusion and hope for Buddha to guide you?

Blame the King of Hell

There was a person who, after death, the King of Hell judged him guilty according to the evil deeds he had done. That person said: "If only I had known this earlier, it would have been different. Why didn't Your Majesty tell me sooner that this day would come?"

King of Hell replied: "I have told you the news many times. Wrinkled skin is the first news. Loose teeth are falling out is the second news. Weakness of strength is the third news. Deaf ears and blurred eyes are the fourth and fifth news. So I have told people too many times. then."

At that time, someone died young in the palace, so he cried and said: "Such news is only for him, but I really don't have it."

King of Hell said: "That's not true, you also had many news. Remember when you were a child, did you ever hear of someone dying from an illness or an epidemic? Have you ever heard of someone dying from a wound?

strangling? Have you ever heard of someone being harmed by fire, drifting water, wild animals, or bitten by poisonous snakes and dying? All of these things are information for you, there is no need to wait for your name to be called correctly to inform you? must also pay respect and worship, only in this way can only those who recite Buddha's name be reborn.

The moth

The moth dies in the flame of a lamp, that death is not really because of the fire, but because of its attachment. When people are afraid of its death and feel sorry for it and reach out to chase it away, it tries to find a gap to crawl in, because it believes that its clinging views are right, certainly not wrong. That's why it was determined to rush forward, even if it died, it was not afraid.

People living in this world like sounds, shapes, money, possessions, gambling, alcohol... that's where their attachments are, so they only pay attention to those things. That's why I'm determined to run and chase, even if I die, I'm not afraid. Why don't you borrow that moth's mirror and look at yourself?

The stupid fly in the window

There was a fly inside the window covered with paper, struggling to fly back and forth all day long but still unable to escape. That's because it clings too tightly to its own attachments, and just keeps flying forward without taking a step back to find another way.

If you can take a step back, every place will be spacious and open. This Saha world is no different from a large window covered with paper. From ancient times until now, it is unknown how many foolish flies have been tightly trapped inside it.

How lucky we are today, to be able to take a step back and see the wide open path to the Western Pure Land, so that we can fly away. How refreshing and exciting it was to fly back to the West!

Four ways to tame horses

During Buddha's time, there was a person who was very good at taming horses. The Buddha asked him what method he used, he replied that he used four methods. The first is to give grace, the second is to show authority, the third is to first show authority and then give grace and the fourth is to first give grace and then show authority.

Buddha asked: "If using all four of those methods still cannot be tamed, then what should I do?" The horse trainer replied: "The only way is to kill them."

Then he asked: "World-Honored One! What method do you use to educate sentient beings?"

Buddha replied: "The Buddha also uses four methods. The first is to give grace, which is to teach them to learn the way of practice for good people who have faith. The second is to use authority, that is, to teach the rotation in the three evil paths for those who often do evil, so that they will be afraid and not do evil anymore. The third is to first teach them to learn the path and practice, [then bring the rotation in the three evil paths to remind and encourage their practice.] Fourth is to bring out the cycle of the three evil paths, show them fear, [then teach them the way to practice.]

The horse trainer asked: "If using all four methods but still cannot be taught, what should I do?"

Buddha said: "Also kill."

The horse trainer asked: "The Tathagata is so compassionate and compassionate, why would he kill?" people?”

Great Master Tuan Thuc was revered by his contemporaries as Master Tu Van Sam, lived in the Song Dynasty, and was from Taizhou, Lam Hai District. He studied the deeds of the ancients and became famous throughout both the Zhejiang and Zhexi regions.

did not sleep at night,1 the skin under both feet was torn, and continuously vomited blood. Zen Master Vien Chieu Tong Ban

Zen Master Tong Ban lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Wuxi district, Changzhou. At first, he studied with Zen master Thien Y Nghia Hoai. While reciting the Buddha's name, he was somewhat enlightened. After that, he moved to Tinh Tu, then served the edict to the Eastern Kinh, and entered the king's palace to lecture on the essentials of meditation. However, every day he still silently practiced following the Pure Land.

Dharma Master Loi Phong once reached the Pure Land in a trance, saw a beautiful lotus flower and asked, someone replied: "That flower is waiting for Zen Master Tong Ban to be born."

Once again Tu Phuc Hy Cong came to worship him and then offered gold, someone asked the reason, he said:

"I entered meditation and saw a yellow lotus flower, some said it was waiting for Mr. Tong Ban to be reborn. I also saw countless other lotuses, some of which were withered, some said: Those are people who have turned their minds to depravity. Then I immediately asked: Mr. Tong Ban originally practiced Zen Buddhism, why was he named in the Pure Land? Someone replied: Although he was in Zen Buddhism, he still practiced Pure Land."

Later, at the time of his death, he calmly sat down and passed away. The king gave him the name Vien Chieu Zen Master.

Master Cuu Phap Hoa

Master Kha Cuu lived in the Song Dynasty, residing in Minh Chau. He often chanted the Lotus Sutra and vowed to be reborn in the Pure Land, so people called him the Great Master Cuu Phap Hoa.

In the 8th year of Nguyen Huu,1 the Great Master was 81 years old, and one day he sat upright and passed away. Three days later, he suddenly came back to life and told everyone: "I have seen the Pure Land scene. It is consistent with the description in the scriptures. On each lotus stand there is the name of the person who will be born. I have seen a golden lotus stand with the name of Huan Cong in Quang Giao Institute, Thanh Do Prefecture, there is a stand with the name of Ton Thap Nhi Lang in Minh Chau, another with the name Kha Cuu. In addition, I have seen a silver stand with the name Tu Dao Co in Minh Chau." Having finished speaking, he passed away.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1093.

Five years later, Tu Dao She passed away, and a strange fragrance spread throughout the room.

Twelve years later, Ton Thap Nhi Lang passed away, people heard heavenly music welcoming them, just as the Great Master had foretold.

The fact that the lotus flower in Pure Land has a name, some people are skeptical and think it's hard to believe. But considering that the Great Master sat down and passed away, then came back to life and foretold what would happen many years later, is that not enough to believe?

Nun Dai Minh

Nun Dai Minh lived in the Sui Dynasty. Every time she entered the retreat to worship Buddha, she first changed into clean clothes and held incense in her mouth. Emperor Wen later greatly respected the nun.

On the day the nun passed away, everyone felt the smell of incense spread throughout the room. In a moment, a bright halo suddenly appeared in layers, like clouds, towards the West and then gradually faded.

Nun Tinh Chan

Nun Sister Tinh Chan lived in the Tang Dynasty, stayed at Tich Thien Pagoda, Truong An, dressed in rags, and begged for alms every day.

The nun chanted the Vajra Sutra up to ten thousand times, concentrating on reciting Buddha's name every day. One day, the nun

told her disciple: "In five months I have seen the Buddha ten times, and twice I saw his pupils playing happily on the precious lotus. I was reborn into the highest class."

As soon as the nun finished speaking, she sat cross-legged and solemnly passed away, the light from the wall illuminating the whole room.

Nun Ngo Tanh

Nun Ngo Tanh lived in the Tang Dynasty, lived in Lo Son, practiced the Buddha's name, and persistently vowed to be reborn.

One day, suddenly hearing music in the air, the nun told the disciples around her: "I was reborn in the middle class, seeing like-minded people." To diligently recite the Buddha's name, there are lotus flowers waiting in the Pure Land. Each of you must make your own efforts."

After speaking, he passed away.

Nun Nang Phung

Nun Nang Phung lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Tien Duong. The nun specializes in practicing the Pure Land method and once dreamed of seeing the Buddha's halo shining on her body.

When the nun heard the good sound in the air, she immediately said to her disciples: "It is time for me to pass away."

In a moment, the disciples suddenly heard the nun's powerful chant of Buddha's name. Looking back, they saw her sitting still with her hands clasped facing the West before passing away. A strange fragrance spread throughout the room. There was music that gradually moved to the West and then disappeared.

Bhikkhu Phap Tang

Nanny Phap Tang lived during the Song Dynasty, in Jinling. The nun is diligent and determined to recite Buddha's name, not caring about external matters.

One night, the nun saw Amitābha Buddha and the Bodhisattvas coming, the light was shining wonderfully, immediately clasped her hands and recited the Buddha's name and passed away.1

The rebirth story of the king and mandarin

King O-truong2

NOTE 2

The original work used O-truong (烏萇), is a transliteration of the Sanskrit word Udyāna, also read as Australia-dia-lead-na. Master Xuanzang in the Western Records called this country O-truong-na. This is an ancient country in northern India, known to Buddhism from a very early age, but later tended to practice more according to Theravada. Great Master Padmasambhava was from this country and came to teach Dharma in Tibet.

King O-chang, whenever he had some free time after solving thousands of affairs in the country, loved to learn Buddhism. The king often said

to his mandarins: "Even though I enjoy many blessings and pleasures as king, I cannot avoid impermanence. Having heard that the Pure Land of Amitābha Buddha in the West is a place of rest, I vow to be reborn in that realm."

Therefore, the king persevered in practice, day and night six times walking and reciting Buddha's name. Every time the monks made offerings, the king and queen personally took care of the food offerings, and for thirty years they never missed it.

When the king was about to die, his face was bright and happy, everyone saw the Buddha coming to welcome him, along with many good omens.

Wei Crown Prince

Wei Crown Prince of the Song Dynasty, along with his two sons and one daughter who were princesses, all practiced the Pure Land method, only his wife refused to practice.

The princess died early. Seven days after being dead, he suddenly came back to life and told his mother: "I saw that in the seven-jeweled lake in the West, there were lotus flowers waiting for my father and two brothers. In the future, I will be reborn there. Only my mother did not see any lotus flowers, so I temporarily went back to tell her, asking her to soon develop the mind to recite Buddha's name." As soon as he finished speaking, he closed his eyes and died.

The mother took advantage of that and quickly developed faith, chanting Buddha's name tirelessly. Later, their whole family passed away one after another in a quiet, peaceful sitting position, and when they died, they all had many good omens.

Liu Di Min joined the army

During the Jin Dynasty, there was Liu Di Min, a native of Pengcheng, who was a descendant of King So Yuan. Di Dan lost his father at a young age and raised his mother who was famous for her filial piety. Initially accepted the position of Phu Tham Quan, then returned to hiding. Ta An and Liu Du both recommended him, but he did not accept the invitation. He went to Lo Son to join Master Tue Vien's Bach Lien commune. He concentrated and persevered in reciting Buddha's name, spending a long time without ever being lazy.

He was once meditating and suddenly saw Buddha's halo illuminating the ground, turning yellow. After staying in the mountain for fifteen years, he saw Amitābha Buddha emitting light from between his eyebrows, then reaching out to comfort him. He clasped his hands and prayed earnestly: "May Tathagata use his hand to caress my head and use his robe to cover my body." As soon as the prayer ended, the Buddha immediately rubbed his head and covered his body with his robe.

One ​​night, he dreamed of Amitābha Buddha with a halo around his head and a swastika on his chest. He pointed at the water in the lake with all eight merits, telling him to drink it. Di Dan drank the water and found it delicious. When he woke up, suddenly there was a strange scent emanating from his pores. He immediately told everyone: "The Pure Land of Grace has arrived."

He immediately lit incense in front of the Buddha statue and prayed: "Thanks to listening to the teachings of Śākyamuni Buddha, I learned that Amitābha Buddha exists. Now I vow to offer this incense, first to Śākyamuni Buddha, then to Amitābha Buddha, along with the Sutra

The Lotus Flower of Wonderful Dharma. May all sentient beings be born in the Pure Land." After praying, he clasped his hands, faced the West, and passed away.

District Lieutenant Ma Tu Van

Ma Tu Van lived in the Tang Dynasty, was recommended to the filial piety,1 received the position of District Lieutenant. One time, he brought people's tax money back to the capital to hand it over. In a strong wind, the boat sank and lost everything, and he was immediately arrested.

NOTE 1
