These are filial and incorruptible people, collectively known as filial piety. After being recommended, they will be appointed to official positions.

During his time in prison, he focused on reciting Buddha's name, and after 5 years he was immediately pardoned and released. From there, he went to Nam Lang Son Pagoda to live in seclusion, concentrating on practicing.

One ​​day, he was not sick, and suddenly said to the people around him: "I have been diligently reciting Buddha's name all my life, now my pure karma has been achieved, and I am about to be reborn in the Pure Land."

The next day, he bathed, changed into clean clothes, and sat neatly with his hands clasped and reciting Buddha's name. Suddenly, a strange scent spread throughout the room. He happily said: "Buddha has come to pick me up." As soon as he finished speaking, he passed away.

Tutor Zhang Di

Zhang Di lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Qiantang. He became an assistant teacher and received the Bodhisattva precepts with

Lawyer Vien Tinh. He learned about the Pure Land method and then determined to practice it, vowing to be reborn in the Pure Land.

Every time he recites Buddha's name, he tries his best to recite clearly, until the sound stops. One day, he told Venerable Vien Tinh: "I was in meditation and saw a white bird flying right before my eyes."

Three years later, he sat upright, facing the West, peacefully reciting Buddha's name, and passed away.

Dr. Wang Longshu

Wang Nhat Xiu lived in the Song Dynasty, a native of Longshu. He was an upright, simple but pure person, well-versed in history and scriptures.

One ​​day, he took all the books in the house and threw them away, saying: "These are all karmic habits, not the ultimate method. From now on, I am determined to head towards the Western Pure Land."

From then on, he diligently recited Buddha's name. At the age of 60, he still wore rough clothes, ate poorly, bowed to Buddha a thousand times a day, and only lay down to sleep in the middle of the night.

He composed a Pure Land essay to advise people to practice the Buddhist recitation method.1

NOTE 1

Lo Cong Van Ngan Bac

Van Ngan Bac lived in the Song Dynasty, believed deeply in the Three Jewels, and specialized in practicing the Buddha's name. During the time he resided in the capital, together with Dharma Master Tinh Nghiem, he established a Buddhist recitation conference, the number of people participating in the teachings reached up to ten thousand people. Young Master Chung Ly

the family has not broken the precept of killing for seven generations. He had a profound understanding of the principles of Zen Buddhism, but directed his mind toward the Pure Land. He previously wrote the book Truc Chi Pure Land, 3 volumes, widely advising people to recite Buddha's name.

Buddha, the older he gets, the more diligent he becomes. One day, he suddenly looked up into the sky and said: "Buddha is coming to pick me up." He immediately clasped his hands in reverence and passed away.

Trinh Muc Khanh

Trinh Muc Khanh lived in the Tang Dynasty, his whole family practiced the Buddha's name. Around the reign of Khai Nguyen, he was seriously ill. Someone advised him to eat fish, but he refused.

At that time, he held the incense burner in his hand, vowing to be reborn. Suddenly, a strange fragrance spread throughout, and he quietly and peacefully passed away.

Nguyen Tu Tai

Nguyen Tu Tai lived in the Tang Dynasty, residing at the temple

Avalokitesvara, Nhuan Chau. He understood the Amitabha Sutra and practiced the Buddha's name.

Sun Liang

Sun Liang lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Qiantang. He went into seclusion to read the Sutras in the Tripitaka, deeply understanding the essence of the Avatamsaka Sutra.

He relied on Lawyer Dai Tri to receive the Bodhisattva precepts, focusing on reciting the Buddha's names ten thousand times a day, for twenty years without stopping.

When the monks had gathered and had not been reciting the Buddha's name for long, he suddenly looked up into the air, clasped his hands and said: "The Buddha and the Bodhisattva sitting on the lotus throne have arrived." and passed away, with a strange fragrance spreading. After cremation, 108 small pea-sized relics were obtained.

Ton Trung

Ton Trung lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Tu Minh. He soon admired the practice of reciting Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the West, and built a Buddhist temple.

Later, when he was sick, he invited a hundred monks to recite Buddha's name. Right while reciting the Buddha's name, he suddenly raised his hands to the sky, his face looked happy, peaceful and passed away.

People in the city at that time heard heavenly music, a strange scent, gradually headed to the West and then disappeared.

He had two children who were also dedicated to reciting Buddha's name, and later they both sat peacefully and passed away.

Tham Thuyen

Tham Thuyen lived in the Song Dynasty, lived in Tien Duong, and with his wife surnamed Thi dedicatedly practiced the Pure Land dharma. Every day, whatever good deed you do, dedicate it to the Western Pure Land.

Later, when he and his wife passed away one after another, they both felt a Buddha appear to welcome them, and heavenly music echoed.

The Luong Street

One ​​day, when he was not sick, he suddenly said: "Buddha came to pick me up." After saying this, he bowed, and as soon as he finished, he passed away.

Luc Jun

On his deathbed, he invited lawyer Vien Tinh to come and explain about the Western Pure Land, chanting the Sutra1 as soon as he reached Pham Thuong, Mr. Vien Tinh said: "You can go now." diligently recited Buddha's name, and the whole family respectfully followed the Buddha's teachings.

When he was about to die, he knew the date and time in advance, changed into solemn clothes, said goodbye to everyone, and then peacefully passed away.

Ngo Mao lived during the Qing Dynasty and was a servant of Ngo Luc Phong in Thanh Duong district. He is a person who maintains the precepts, often does good deeds, and concentrates on reciting Buddha's name constantly.

Vuong Manh Lan and Trinh Sinh

Vuong Manh Lan is a descendant of Confucian scholars in Con Son, a life of teaching, and an honest personality without deception. He gave birth to a son named Tuong Than, worshiping

parents are extremely filial. Vuong Manh Lan only worried about reciting Buddha's name all day, not worrying about other things.

At the beginning of winter in the 41st year of Kangxi's reign,1 he was over 70 years old and had a slight illness. In early November, I went to visit,2 Vuong Manh Lan said: "People in the world still take the 17th of this month as the birthday of Amitābha Buddha. I will go on that day." To Ky Son

To Ky Son is from Con Son, his real name is Khoi Phung. All his life he kept the precept of not killing, even if he saw insects, he did not hurt him.

In his old age, he dedicated himself to cultivating the Pure Land. While walking, standing, lying, and sitting, he always maintained the chant of Buddha's name, without interruption. In the year of the Cat of the Kangxi era,1 he was 80 years old. When the weather was too cold, he wrapped himself in a blanket and sat reciting Buddha's name. Around noon on November 26, he told his grandson Dien Phuong: "The cause and effect of the Pure Land has matured, so three days ago I saw Buddha appear, but I didn't want to tell you. Tonight, at the hour of the Rat, I will be reborn."

After that, he got up, changed his clothes, lit a lamp, burned incense, sat upright facing the West, and asked his family members to recite Buddha's name together to help him reborn. Just before the third watch, I heard the sound of his reciting the Buddha's name fading away, then quietly passed away.

Ngo Kinh Son

Ngo Kinh Son is from the same village as To Ky Son, and is a fellow practitioner in the Buddha recitation group. When he was over 70 years old, he became interested in studying Buddhism. At the last moment, he sat peacefully and passed away. He specifically told me to come and thank him for advising him to recite the Buddha's name."

Vuong Quan Vinh

Vuong Quan Vinh is from Thai Thuong, Con Son. Since he was a child, he has practiced the precepts and learned the teachings of Buddhism, which are truly sublime and sublime. Later, he practiced the Pure Land method, reciting Buddha's name ten thousand times a day, regardless of whether the weather was hot or cold, without interruption.

In the 56th year of Khang Hy's reign,1 on August 2, he knew in advance that he was about to die, so he invited Elder Kien Hanh at Tinh Danh hermitage to come, wanting him to explain and prove it. Right at noon, teacher Kien Hanh said: "Why don't you leave it for tomorrow?" Quan Vinh replied: "I have decided to go today." He immediately told him to bring pen and paper, wrote a verse to leave behind, and told his daughter to prepare the coffin. Once everything was done, he respectfully clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name and left.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1717.

The girl carried his body into the coffin, but could not lift it up, so she silently prayed and naturally lifted it up gently. That year he was 81 years old.

Rebirth stories of young
year-olds

Two novices

During the Sui Dynasty, there were two novice monks in Wenzhou who both practiced the Buddha's name. One day, the older monk suddenly passed away. Seeing that he had come to the Pure Land to meet the Buddha, he immediately said: "There is a younger novice monk practicing with me, will he be able to be reborn?" The Buddha taught: "It was that novice who advised you, so you made up your mind to practice reciting the Buddha's name. Now you can return to Saha, make more efforts to practice, and three years later you two will be reborn here together."

[The older novice then revived, the two of them

continued to diligently practice.] Three years later, both of them saw the Buddha appear, the earth shook, there were flowers from the sky falling and flying, the two novices passed away at the same time.

The student wants to be reborn

Great Master Duy Ngan lived in the Tang Dynasty, practiced the Pure Land Repentance Dharma, and was diligent and diligent without getting tired. One day, the Great Master saw two Bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta appearing in mid-air. The great master was so happy that he wanted to find an artist to paint that scene. Suddenly two people came and said they could draw and agreed to draw. After drawing, both disappeared. The great master immediately told his disciples: "Today I am reborn, does anyone want to go with me?"

Among them was a child who wanted to be reborn with him. The Great Master immediately told him to go home and say goodbye to his parents. Parents thought it was a joke and didn't believe it. Moments later, the boy showered, changed his clothes, and sat upright, reciting the Buddha's name and rebirth first. That great master called someone to bring paper and pen and write a poem of praise. After writing the verse, the Great Master peacefully sat down and passed away.

Su Tan

Su Tan lived in the Song Dynasty, was from Ung Chau, and became a monk at a young age. At the age of 14, he practiced reciting Buddha's name without stopping. Suddenly he fell ill and died suddenly. He revived in an instant and told his teacher and parents: "Amitābha Buddha is here, I will follow him."

At that time, everyone in the neighborhood saw a precious lotus flower appear in mid-air, with a halo of five unusual colors, appearing and then fading towards the West.

Ha Dam Tich

Ha Dam Tich lived in the Yuan Dynasty, at the age of 18 maintained the Bodhisattva precepts, and concentrated on reciting Buddha's name all day. One day, just after waking up at the fourth hour, his family said it was too early. Dam Tich said: "I saw Buddha and Bodhisattva in the middle of nowhere, there were flags and garlands coming to welcome them." Having said that, sit quietly and walk away.

The Ngo family1

At the age of 16, the mandarin in charge of distributing labor wages

he immediately used that money to buy incense to worship Buddha and then knelt down and recited Amitabha's holy name. The next day, he came before the Admiral and said the same thing. The admiral was angry, ordered him to be taken to the officer in charge, and sentenced him to 15 strokes of the cane. The day came, around the fifth watch, he woke up, washed himself, burned incense to worship Buddha, and still went to the boat officer in charge to say goodbye. The mandarin was angry, sent soldiers to follow him, and when he arrived, he saw Mr. Ngo turn to the West, bow three times, then sit upright reading verses. After reading the verse, he immediately breathed Samadhi fire and burned his body. When the military officials saw it from afar, they all started to pay respect and worship. The officer in charge then immediately closed the door and fasted to keep the precepts. The mandarin wrote a poem praising Mr. Ngo:

The body wears iron armor,
The feet step on a lotus flower.

This verse not only praises Mr. Ngo, but it seems that the mandarin wrote it with the intention of blaming himself for being disrespectful to the true monk. But the book Pure Land Thanh Hien Luc Tien Bien (淨土聖賢錄續編) does not have this verse, but copies the verse Mr. Ngo read before rebirth, which in our opinion has a more appropriate content. And it seems that one of these two verses was mistakenly copied as the other, because the details in the verse are very similar. The verse before Mr. Ngo's death was as follows: 身在營中心出 家。身披鎧甲是袈裟。刀刀親見彌陀佛。箭箭射著白蓮華。 (Body at Camp Zhong) The mind is a monk, the body is not armored with a ka-sa. Roughly translated: The body is in the military, the mind is a monk, the body is wearing armor, the ka-sa. The story of a woman's rebirth

Empress Tuy Van De

Empress of Sui Van De, surnamed Doc Co, although in the royal palace, was tired of leaving her female body, often chanting Amitābha Buddha's name, praying to be reborn in the Pure Land.

On Giap Ty day in August,1 the queen passed away, a strange fragrance spread throughout the palace, all natural musical instruments echoed everywhere. The emperor asked Sardi-tu-na why there was such a good omen. He replied: "The Queen specializes in Pure Land cultivation and was reborn in the Buddha's country, so that is a good omen."

NOTE 1

Wen Jingwen's wife

Wen Jingwen lived in the Tang Dynasty, his wife was from Jingzhou, and was sick. bedridden for a long time. Wen Jingwen advised her to recite Buddha's name. She believed and immediately concentrated on reciting Buddha's name for a year.

One ​​day, she suddenly saw the holy land of the Pure Land and immediately said to Wen Jingwen: "I have seen Buddha, I will go next month." She also said goodbye and told her parents, [advising them to recite Buddha's name so that] together they could be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. On that day, she passed away peacefully.

Mrs. Ly

Ms. Ly in Ho Mon lived in the Song Dynasty and was from Thuong Ngu. After mourning her husband, she devoted herself early and late to reciting Buddha's name and chanting the Amitabha Sutra, persevering for more than ten years.

One ​​day, she met a monk wearing a red parasol and said: "At the hour of the hour, on the next full moon day, you will be reborn." Mrs. Ly asked who the teacher was, and the monk replied: "You often chant my name."

Mrs. Ly said goodbye to all her relatives, sat upright on the same day and time, and passed away peacefully. Everyone around saw a very strange light, shining so brightly that it was blinding. After seven days of cremation, the six senses were still intact. After the cremation, we saw too many relics to count. Then one day, the place where the body was cremated suddenly grew a flower, shaped like a white poppy.

The Trinh family

The Trinh family member lived in the Song Dynasty, was from Tien Duong, chanted the Pho Mon sutra every day, and often recited Buddha's name.

Later, she got sick and told her family to take a bath. After bathing, sit facing the west and ask your family: "Do you hear the sound of opening ceremony? Buddha and Bodhisattva are coming soon." After a moment, he happily said: "Buddha and Bodhisattva have both arrived." Having finished speaking, he clasped his hands in reverence and passed away.

Lady of the surname Vuong

King Kinh of the Song Dynasty, there was a lady of the surname Vuong, dedicated to cultivating the Pure Land, morning and night, extremely diligent. The servants all followed the example of practice, only one concubine was often lazy and lazy. The lady reprimanded her, and she immediately woke up and practiced diligently.

Later, that concubine suddenly died without being sick, telling another concubine in a dream: "Thanks to your wife's teachings, I have now been reborn in the Pure Land." The lady still couldn't believe it when she heard the story. Not long after, the lady also dreamed that she and her concubine were walking by the treasure pond, seeing a lotus flower with a flying sky-cloth, with the name Duong Kiet written on it; Another flower has a figure wearing court clothes sitting on it, with the name Ma Vu written on it. Seeing a golden lotus with a bright halo of light, the other concubine pointed at it and said: "This is the place where you will be born."

After waking up from her dream, Lady Vuong became even more diligent in her practice. At the age of 81, on the morning of her birthday, the people around her were just about to hold a ceremony to celebrate her longevity when she held an incense lamp in her hand in front of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara statue, stood upright and passed away.

Trieu officials requested1 Vuong Du. She often chanted the Lotus Sutra, wholeheartedly devoted herself to the Pure Land dharma. Each time she repented, she recited the Buddha's name ten thousand times, persevering like that for thirty years.

One ​​day, suddenly she heard the sound of a sky drum ringing by itself, everyone around her felt unusually surprised, then at that moment she sat upright, facing the West, made a seal with her hands, and passed away peacefully.

The Gong family

The Gong family lived in the Song Dynasty, a member of the Tang Dynasty, day and night dedicated to reciting Buddha's name and chanting the Amitabha Sutra.

Later, when she became ill, she invited Lawyer Hanh to come and teach. Before everything was arranged, she sat upright, peacefully, and passed away.

Some old concubines saw this and concentrated on reciting Buddha's name. One day, suddenly in a dream, Mrs. Cung said: "I have been born in the Pure Land, in seven days you will also be reborn."

On that day, indeed, the old concubine passed away peacefully without illness.

Hang's grandmother

Hang's grandmother lived in the Song Dynasty, her name was Dieu Tri.

Her husband died, she took care of raising two daughters, and later both became monks.

She diligently recites Buddha's name diligently. At the time of her death, a strange fragrance spread throughout the house. She turned her face to the West, made a seal with her hands, smiled and passed away.

The surname Bui

The surname Bui lived in the Song Dynasty, in Fenyang, and was dedicated and persistent in reciting Buddha's name, regardless of whether the weather changed from hot or cold, without interruption. When dying, call family members to bring fire to burn incense and say: "Buddha brings a lotus flower to welcome me, I am about to be reborn." As soon as she finished speaking, she suddenly saw flowers falling from the sky, she sat upright, peacefully and passed away.

The Tram family

The Tram family lived in the Song Dynasty and since childhood was a vegetarian and recited Buddha's name. After getting married, she became a daughter-in-law in the Chuong family, often helping hungry people.

Later, she had a mild illness and became even more diligent in her efforts to recite Buddha's name. One day she saw the Bodhisattvas, gods and saints appearing before her eyes, and immediately left peacefully that day.

Grandma Sun

Grandma Sun lived in the Song Dynasty, lived in Tu Minh, and was widowed. She focused and persevered in reciting Buddha's name for 30 years without delay.

Later, she had a mild illness and dreamed that she was repenting with eight monks. When he woke up, he immediately took a bath, changed his clothes, and invited the monks to come to the repentance ceremony. She sat upright and recited sutras in front of the crowd, until her mind was calm and she made a seal with her left hand and left. At that time, people near and far could clearly hear music in the air.

The Lau family

Lady Lau lived in the Song Dynasty, had a calm personality, had intelligence, and married Tu Bac Chu Nguyen Khanh. She once studied the book Truyen Dang Luc, and at some points she understood and became enlightened. From then on, he turned even more towards the Pure Land method, focusing on reciting Buddha's name non-stop.

In her old age, she fell ill and suddenly saw a purple lotus flower and countless transformed Buddhas. At that time, a strange scent spread throughout the house. She immediately told her family members to quickly recite Buddha's name and help her. Just a few minutes later, he sat upright, calm and quiet.

The Qin lady

The Qin lady lived in the Song Dynasty, had a steadfast personality, liked cleanliness, hated being a woman, followed her husband to many places, and was persistent in being professional.

She often reads the Avatamsaka Sutras, Dharma Flower Sutras, Golden Light Sutras, and Prajnaparamita Sutras, never letting a day go by in vain. Every day, morning and night, he practiced Amitabha Dharma repentance and bowed to Buddha up to a thousand times.

Later, she saw a halo of light shining into the house, immediately sat upright, facing the West, and passed away.

The Liang family

The Liang family lived in the Song Dynasty, lived in Fenyang, was blind in both eyes, and fortunately met a monk who advised him to recite Buddha's name, and she listened.

After three years, her eyes suddenly brightened again. Later, she saw Buddha and Bodhisattva, banners and precious parasols coming to welcome them, and immediately sat upright that day and passed away.

Grandma Tuong

Grandma Tuong lived in the Qing Dynasty and was from Hung Hoa. At the age of 40, her husband died. After the funeral, she cried and told her son: "When impermanence comes, no one can replace each other. For example, today my mother also died, and I could not bear it, but I don't know what to do. From now on, I will devote myself to being a vegetarian and reciting Buddha's name, not caring about anything else."

The son obeyed his mother and immediately built a thatched hut right next to the house. She lives in a hermitage, closes the door and specializes in reciting Buddha's name, regardless of whether the weather is hot or cold, she doesn't care.

After 5 years, in the year of Canh Ty in the Thuan Tri era,1 on May 20, she suddenly told her child: "Today I can buy wood to make a coffin. At noon on the next 23rd, I will return to the Western Pure Land."

NOTE 1

That is the year 1660, the 17th year of Thuan Tri.

Then she went to say goodbye to all the neighbors. On that day, she peacefully recited Buddha's name and left. Then he also set fire to Samadhi himself to burn the coffin.

The Ha family

The Ha family lived in the Qing Dynasty, lived in Ty Lang, and was the wife of layperson Phan Huong Cao. Huong Cao wholeheartedly believed in Buddha and together with Mrs. Ha practiced the Pure Land dharma. Every day she chants the Diamond Sutra, early and late at night she often worships, recites the Buddha's name, and prays to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

In the seventh month of the year Canh Than in the reign of Khang Hy,1 she fell ill and foretold that at noon on the 29th of that month she would be reborn.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1680, the 19th year of the Kangxi era.

On the right day, all her sons and daughters returned, and invited good friends to come. They all recited Buddha's name in unison, and she clasped her hands and departed peacefully.

The surname Luc

The surname Luc from Thai Thuong, Kun Son, is the wife of Truong Quy Tu from Dai Tay, Quan Ngoai. Since the age of 17, he has been a vegetarian, practiced reciting Buddha's name, chanted the Diamond Sutra, and the Great Compassion Mantra, all dedicated to praying for rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Whenever I see others killing animals, I vow to save them.

In September of the 42nd year of Kangxi,2 she suddenly saw in the air many boats and palanquins going to the West, and the people carrying the palanquins and rowing the boats were all monks. Less than three days later, she peacefully recited Buddha's name and left on September 26.

NOTE 2

That was the year 1703.

The rebirth story of evil
people who repented

Truong Thien Hoa

Truong Thien Hoa lived in the Tang Dynasty, working as a buffalo slaughterer for a living. When he was about to die, he saw a herd of buffaloes that could speak human language and followed him demanding his life. Thien Hoa was so frightened that he called his wife and said: "Quickly invite a monk to come and repent for me."

The monk invited to teach Truong Thien Hoa: "The scriptures say: People who are about to die see evil and evil appearances. If they sincerely recite Buddha's name, they will immediately be reborn." Thien Hoa said: "Hell is coming soon, there is no time to get an incense burner." Immediately use your right hand to hold the fire, chant incense with your left hand, and turn your face to the West to recite Buddha's name. After reciting for less than ten hours, he suddenly said to himself: "Buddha is coming to pick me up." Having finished speaking, he passed away.

Oanh Kha

Oanh Kha was born in the Song Dynasty. Although she became a monk, she did not abstain from alcohol and meat. Thinking to myself, I am already a monk and if I do such bad and bad things, I will have to suffer in the future. What can I do? Ask someone who lives with you to bring you the book Van Sinh Sinh Story to read. Reading each story, I felt moved in my heart, then I sat facing the West, focused on reciting Buddha's name, and skipped eating and drinking.

After three days, in a dream, Buddha said:

“You still have ten more years to live, try your best.” Oanh Kha told Buddha: "The world of Jambudvipa is full of evil, it is easy to lose mindfulness, I vow to be born in the Pure Land sooner, to serve the saints." Buddha taught: "If so, then after three days I will pick you up."

The day came, Oanh Kha invited the crowd to chant the Amitabha Sutra, and later said: "Buddha and the crowd have all arrived." Having said that, he passed away peacefully.

Trống Minh

Trống Minh lived in the Song Dynasty, practiced at Bao An pagoda in Son Am, and could not strictly keep the precepts.

One ​​day, Trong Minh fell ill and told his fellow practitioner, Dao Ninh: "My mind is extremely scattered, how can I treat it?" Dao Ninh advises focusing on reciting Buddha's name with your breath. Trong Minh listened to the words and wholeheartedly recited Buddha's name.

After seven days, Trong Minh was exhausted. Dao Ninh taught him how to visualize the Buddha image right before his eyes. Trong Minh meditated for a long time, suddenly saw two Bodhisattvas, then saw Buddha, then closed his eyes and passed away.

Comment

If evil people can be reborn, it is thanks to the Buddha's mind that is a hundred times more powerful than normal, so they can achieve success in ten recitations. If you don't do that, just a little delay and you will stumble and fall into the three evil paths.

The story of the rebirth of animals

The rebirth of the dragon

The Bodhisattva Sutra on the treatment of fetuses says: “There was a dragon who said to the golden bird: ‘Since I was born as a dragon, I have never killed or disturbed living beings. live in the country. After my death, I will be born in the Pure Land of Amitābha Buddha. When he was about to die, the bird recited Buddha's name for ten times and then died. At the cremation, more than a dozen relics were found, the light was dazzling and dazzling.

NOTE 1

That is between the years 785 and 805, during the reign of King Duc Tong.

Great Master Tue Quan immediately built a tower for the birds, and Doan Vi Cao wrote the inscription in the capital.

The rebirth of the starling

During the Song Dynasty, Quan Cong at Chanh Dang Pagoda in Hoang Nham raised a starling and taught him to speak human language. Birds often recite Buddha's name constantly.

One ​​day, the bird stood dead in the cage. Quan Cong dug a grave for burial. Not long after, a purple lotus flower grew from the tip of the bird's tongue.

Dam Chau also has a person who raises a starling, can talk, and often recites Buddha's name. After the flute died, that person

also built a coffin for burial like a human. Suddenly, a lotus flower grew from the grave. Looking down to the root, I saw that lotus flower growing from the bird's mouth.

Great Master Lien Tri said: "Parrots and starlings, people teach them that reciting Buddha's name is also a common thing. Why don't we see birds reborn anymore? Alas, just like people in the world, we can listen to the teachings of reciting Buddha's name, but some people recite with a sincere heart, while others recite with a careless, disdainful mind. Therefore, there are many people reciting Buddha's name, but very few people are reborn. As for parrots and starlings, there is no difference. Where?”

Appendix: Story of Layman Thang Lien

Layman Thang Lien's family name is La, his real name is Duan Mai, from Lau Dong.

At first he took the title of layman Vo Thien, why was he later called layman Thang Lien?

Originally, in the fall of the 40th year of Khang Hy's reign, La Duan Mai was critically ill. He was about to write a poem to leave before his death. Suddenly, he heard a voice in the air saying: "The lay practitioner Thang Lien still has another2 century to live, there is no need to write a poem." After that, his illness quickly improved. His relatives all thought it was strange, and from then on they all called him Thang Lien layperson.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1701.

NOTE 2

A century means 12 years.

While pregnant with him, the father dreamed that a monk came to stay in the house, one day immediately

was born as a layman. Because of that, the father soon knew that lay people were people with good roots many generations ago.

By the time he was 4 or 5 years old, he could still remember the appearance, neighborhood and residence of his previous parents. One day, he playfully ran around the pillar many times. He became dizzy and fell down, and his mother beat him. He cried and went to sleep. When he woke up, he couldn't remember anything. Therefore, we know that the history books recording the previous lives of Duong Thuc Tu, Dong Thanh Kien, and To Dong Pha are true and not false.

Since following his teacher to learn how to read, he no longer plays around or follows the habits of teenagers of the same age. Every day he studied and improved very quickly, everyone was confident that he would achieve academic success. But his father, La Tich Chi, saw that he was often sick, so he took pity on him and did not let him take the exam. The layman skillfully understood his parents' wishes, so although he pursued a career as a poet, he did not seek fame and success, only wrote a book to please himself. The book Hoang Diep Thao was written by him, taking the principle of revealing one's character into literature such as Ly and Do.1

NOTE 1

Literature such as Ly and Do: refers to Ly Bach and Du Phu, both famous poets of the Tang Dynasty.

From childhood, he was interested in Taoist nutrition techniques. Later, he went to study with Elder Bich Nham and thoroughly understood the essence of Zen Buddhism. Since La Tich Chi passed middle age, he shouldered all the housework, did not let his parents worry, and devoted himself to taking care of him until the end of his life. His filial piety is truly second to none.

In the fall of the 52nd year of Kangxi's reign,1 layperson Thang Lien fell ill again, and when he knuckled his hands, he calculated that the period of one century (12 years) had expired. Everyone was afraid, but the lay people didn't care at all.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1713.

Previously, in this locality, very few people practiced the Pure Land. Lay people proposed to establish an Intercommune so that everyone could gather together to recite Buddha's name, with up to three or four places. Since then, there have been many people reciting Buddha's name. APPENDIX
ADVICE TEXT
GEVELING THE BODHIC MIND

The foolish and incompetent ordinary monk is Tru Hien,1 now crying and bleeding from the eyes, bowing down, heartbroken and offering words to the present public, along with all good men and women. We hope you will open your hearts to compassion, pay attention and listen carefully.

NOTE 1

This essay was originally written by the Great Master Am Province. The great master's name was That Hien, alias Tu Te, alias Tinh Am, born in 1685 and passed away in 1734.

Often heard that, the gateway to the True Path, the most important development of mind; Urgent matters on the path of practice are nothing more than making vows. Once the vow is established, it is possible to save sentient beings. Once the mind has arisen, Buddhahood will be achieved. If you do not develop a broad mind and make solid vows, you will certainly spend countless lifetimes still in the place of reincarnation. Even if you practice, it's over

It's all just a waste of hard work. Therefore, the Avatamsaka Sutra teaches: "Whoever practices wholesome dharmas but forgets the Bodhi mind is called following the karma of demons." [Once you've developed your mind] you've forgotten it, what's more, you haven't developed your mind yet? So know that, if you want to learn according to Tathagata's Dharma, you must first fully develop the Bodhisattva's aspiration, there can be no delay.

But the aspiration is different, with many appearances, if not clearly indicate which direction to follow? Now, for the sake of the public, I would like to briefly say that the development of the mind has eight distinct tendencies: evil, righteous, true, false, large, small, biased and perfect.

What kind of mind is called evil? What is legitimate? What is truthful? What is a lie? What is large? What is small and narrow? What is bias? What is perfection?

There are people who practice without examining their own minds, only knowing how to follow external circumstances, such as seeking profit or fame, pursuing current sensual pleasures or hoping for future retribution. Having such a mind is called evil.

Not seeking profit or fame, nor greedy for pleasure or retribution, just wanting to escape birth and death and achieve Bodhi. Developing a mind like that is called righteous.

Every thought is to pray for Buddha's way, every thought in the mind is to pity and teach sentient beings. Even though we hear that the Buddhist path is profound and long lasting, we still do not lose heart and fear; Seeing sentient beings who are difficult to save doesn't make you feel discouraged or tired. Like climbing a towering mountain, determined to reach the top; Like climbing a huge tower, determined to the very end. Developing such a mind is called sincerity.

Committing a sin and not repenting, committing a mistake and refusing to let it go, appearing pure on the outside, but inside is full of filth. First you start to be diligent, then you become lazy. Although there is some kindness, most of it is interfered with by fame and fortune. Even if you practice good dharma, you will be contaminated by bad karma. Having such an intention is called a lie.

If the Dharma world of sentient beings has not come to an end, their vows still exist. If Bodhi path has not been achieved, their vows are not fulfilled. Developing a mind like that is called great.

Contemplating the three realms as a prison, the cycle of birth and death as a vengeful person, only wanting to quickly save oneself, not daring to think about saving many people. Developing a mind like that is called small and narrow.

If outside of this mind one sees sentient beings, one must vow to be saved, if one sees the Buddha path, one must vow to achieve it. The hard work of practice is not forgotten, knowledge and knowledge are accumulated and not abandoned. Such a mindset is called bias.

If you know that this nature is a sentient being, you should vow to be liberated; This self-nature is the Buddha way, so we wish to achieve it. I do not see any dharma that is separate from this mind and exists by itself. Use a mind as empty as space to make vows as big as space, practice meritorious deeds like space, and attain fruition like space, but in the end

there is no form of space that can be grasped. Developing the mind like that is called perfection.

Once you know clearly the eight differences above, you can judge; Knowing how to judge means knowing how to choose and reject; If you know how to choose and take away, you can develop your mind in the right way.

What is judgment? That means self-judging which of the eight things mentioned above falls into the direction of one's mind. Is it evil or just? Is it true or a lie? Is it big or small? Is it biased or perfect?

What is the choice to take and leave? That is to say, we must give up evil, deceitful, narrow, and biased tendencies, and choose righteous, true, great, and perfect tendencies.

Generating the mind like that can truly be called developing the Bodhi mind.

This Bodhi mind is at the top of all good dharmas, there must be causes and conditions for it to arise. Now we will talk about causes and conditions, briefly there are ten types.

What are the ten causes and conditions for generating Bodhi mind?

- Firstly, because of thinking about the Buddha's profound grace, we develop

mind; - Second, because you think about your parents' gratitude, you should develop your mind; - Third, because I think about the teacher's grace, I should develop my mind; - Fourth, because of thinking about the charity's offerings,

generate the mind;

- Fifth, because we think about the grace of sentient beings, we should develop our mind; - Sixth, because we think about the suffering of birth and death, we should develop our mind; - Seventh, out of respect for one's own spiritual nature, one should develop

mind; - Eighth, in order to repent of bad karma, you should develop your mind; - Ninth, in order to be born in the Pure Land, you should develop your mind; - Tenth, in order to make the Dharma last in the world

for a long time, you should develop your mind.

What is thinking about the Buddha's profound grace?

That is to say that our Tathagata Shakyamuni, from the time he first developed his mind, practiced the Bodhisattva path for us, going through countless lifetimes and suffering all kinds of suffering. When we create bad karma, Buddha feels compassion and uses teaching methods, but we are foolish and refuse to believe. I had to fall into hell, but Buddha felt sorry for me and wanted to suffer for me, but because I had created heavy karma, I couldn't be saved. When we are born as human beings, Buddha uses means to help us cultivate good roots. From life to life, the Buddha's mind is always present with us, never temporarily leaving. When Buddha had just appeared in the world, we were still deep in the sea of ​​karma. Now that we are human, Buddha has entered nirvana. Why do I have to be born in a time when Dharma ends without Buddha? What blessings do I need to be able to become a monk? Because of what karma is it impossible to see the Buddha's golden body? How lucky is it to be able to personally worship the Buddha's relics?

Consider again, if in the past life we ​​did not cultivate good roots, how can we hear the Buddha's Dharma now? If you don't listen to Buddha's teachings, how will you know yourself?

are often grateful to Buddha? With such grace and virtue, high mountains and hills cannot compare. If you do not develop a great mind, practice the Bodhisattva path, build and develop Buddha Dharma, and help save sentient beings, then even if your bones and flesh are broken, you will not be able to repay.

That is the first cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is thinking about the gratitude of parents?

Every time I think of my parents, I feel endless sadness, because they were born and had to endure countless hardships. Ten months of pregnancy, three years of breastfeeding; At night, the wet side of the mother lies down, the wet side of the child rolls, the bitter day the mother swallows, the sweet part of the child, thanks to that, I can now become human. I just hope that I will continue the family's career and continue the path of worship. Now I have chosen the path of becoming a monk, calling myself a Buddhist disciple, shamefully accepting the name of a monk. Don't offer sweet and delicious dishes to your parents, and don't offer them to your ancestors on death anniversaries. The living parents did not take good care of them, and when they died, they could not lead them in a good path. Considering life's work is a great loss, considering religious work is not really useful. If both paths fail, then serious sins are difficult to avoid.

Consider again that there is only one way, which is to constantly practice the Buddha's way, helping sentient beings in the ten directions and three lifetimes. If so, not only parents in one lifetime, but also parents in many lifetimes will be saved; Not only one person's parents, but everyone's parents are also liberated.

That is the second cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is thinking about the teacher's gratitude?

Even though our parents can give birth to us and nurture our bodies, if we don't have teachers to teach us in life, we probably won't know decency; If we didn't have religious teachers, we probably wouldn't be able to understand the Buddha's teachings.

If you don't know decency, you're like an animal. If you don't understand Buddha's teachings, how are you any different from secular people? Now I also know a few things of etiquette, have a brief understanding of the Buddha's teachings, am dressed in a robe, and my body and mind are imbued with virtue. This is all thanks to the teacher's grace.

If you develop a mind to seek small results, you can only benefit yourself. Now if you choose to follow the Mahayana and vow to bring great benefits to all people, all teachers, whether in the world or in the religion, will also receive benefits.

That is the third cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is thinking about the benefactor's offerings?

That is to say that what we do today, everything we need every day, cannot be obtained by ourselves. Rice porridge two meals a day, clothing for all four seasons, when needed by illness, during daily activities, all expenses are obtained from other people's efforts, brought to us for our own consumption.

Others have to use all their strength to cultivate, but still cannot earn enough to eat; And I sit and can't eat, still not satisfied. Others weave and knit, still unable to overcome difficulties and deprivation; As for me, I sit idle, but I have plenty of clothes, and I don't know how to appreciate them. Others

have thatched houses with leafy walls and are in trouble for the rest of their lives; As for me, I have a big house and a spacious yard, quiet all year round.

Others work hard so we can be at ease, can we have peace of mind? Is it reasonable to take other people's resources to improve yourself?

Therefore, if you yourself cannot apply enough compassion and wisdom, do not adorn yourself with both blessings and wisdom, so that all the dharma of faith and giving are benefited by grace, all sentient beings benefit, then even a grain of rice or a thread of silk, as small as that, must be fully compensated, and the bad and evil retribution will be difficult to avoid.

That is the fourth cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is thinking about the grace of sentient beings?

That is to say that we and sentient beings, from countless lives up to now, have often changed in this life and become each other's parents, so we have gratitude towards each other. Now, even though in another life we ​​are confused and dark, we no longer know each other, but logically, if we are grateful, how can we not repay them?

Even though we see furry animals wearing horns today, how do we know that we were never their children before? Even though we see tiny insects today, how do we know that they were not our parents before? It is often seen that children, if they are separated from their parents, cannot remember their appearance when they grow up, let alone their parents in their previous lives, of course they cannot remember them now. For example, if the parents of a previous life are now screaming and crying in hell, tossing and turning in the realm of hungry ghosts, suffering and suffering, who knows? Hungry, thirsty, needy, who can tell us

? Even though we don't see or hear them, of course they are still hoping for help. Only the scriptures can explain this clearly, only the Buddha can teach us about it, but how can those with wrong views know?

Therefore, the Bodhisattva contemplates the place of rebirth, sees that all are parents in the past, are all Buddhas in the future, often thinking of doing beneficial things and repaying kindness.

That is the fifth cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is thinking about the suffering of birth and death?

That means we, along with all sentient beings, have been in samsara for countless lifetimes and have never been liberated. Sometimes in the human world, sometimes in the heavenly realm, sometimes in this world, sometimes in another direction, life and death are countless, ups and downs are fleeting. As soon as he was born in heaven, he immediately became human; Then suddenly he fell into hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. Hell's door opens early and dark, the cold iron cave temporarily leaves again. Climbing the mountain with swords all over his body left no skin left, climbing trees covered with swords all over his body and being mutilated. The hot iron ball does not eliminate hunger, swallow it and your intestines and liver are cooked. Boiling copper water does not quench your thirst. If you drink it, your bones and flesh will be crushed. A sharp saw cuts the body apart, and as soon as it is severed, it is attached again; A strange wind blew past him, he died and then came back to life.

Wild fire filled the city, resounding with terrible screams; cooking in a large cauldron, only the sound of pain is heard in my ears. The frost has just stopped, the body is as pale as a green lotus bunched with pistils; The flesh and blood are exhausted, the body is red and bruised like a crushed lotus root

broken. Life and death in one night, hell goes through ten thousand times; The pain and suffering every day is more than a hundred years longer than the human world. How many times have we forced the prisoners to torture us so tirelessly, but who would believe the Lord Diem's ​​warnings? When you receive punishment, you know it's suffering. Even though you regret it, how can you go back? But after escaping and forgetting all about birth, all the bad karma is still the same!

Using a whip to whip a donkey to make it bleed, who knows that he is beating his mother? Taking a pig to the slaughterhouse, am I about to kill my father? You don't know how to eat your children's flesh, the ancient King Wen was like that.1 Chewing and swallowing your parents is not knowing, all living things are like that. In the past, we loved each other, but now we hate each other; Originally enemies, now they have become flesh and blood of one family. First a mother, now a father, first a father, now a husband. If you remember knowing the story of your past life, you must feel ashamed and humiliated. People with heavenly eyes that see through everything must feel ridiculous and pitiful.

NOTE 1

When King Wen was still imprisoned in Du Ly, King Tru killed his son and gave him cooked meat to eat. Because he wanted to keep his life to accomplish great things, he knew but had to pretend not to know and still eat it. King Tru saw this and thought he was an ordinary person, there was no need to take precautions, thanks to that he escaped death.

The filth gathered into a bundle, nine months in which it was difficult to pass; Blood and pus all the way down, pitifully! Childhood does not know, here and there are indistinguishable; Growing up to understand, desire immediately arises. Not long after, illness and old age came; Soon impermanence called. [The moment of death] wind and fire are chaotic, surrounding the spirit of chaos; The blood is depleted, the outside skin gradually dries. Each hole

pore is like a needle piercing the flesh; His eyes, nose, and mouth were all like knives. When a turtle has cooked gills, pulling the meat out of its shell is still easy, compared to the dying consciousness leaving the body, much more difficult.

This mind has no permanent subject, like a merchant traveling everywhere as a stranger. This body has no fixed shape, just like a house that often moves here and there. This body has gone back and forth between samsara so many times, [counting it out], the number of dust particles in the great thousand realms cannot be compared. Every tear shed, [collected all together] the waves of the four seas are not as many. Bones have been accumulated for many generations, even though the mountains are high, they still cannot match them. The body was once left in the six realms, spread out all over the earth. For example, if one cannot listen to Buddha's teachings, who sees and hears such things? When you haven't read the scriptures, how can you understand such arguments clearly?

If we continue to be as attached as before, our ignorance is no different from before, we are only afraid that in eons and thousands of lives, if we are wrong once, we will be wrong a hundred times again. This human body is difficult to gain and easy to lose. Life passes so quickly that it is impossible to hold on to it. Then the road ahead is dark, once parting is deep. Bad karma in the three evil paths, do it yourself. There's no way to explain the pain, who knows who can accept it for me? Speaking of this, how can you not shiver in fear?

Therefore, we must end the stream of birth and death, escape the ocean of craving, save ourselves and others, and reach the shore of enlightenment. Elaborate achievements over long lifetimes depend on this one-time decisive effort.

That is the sixth cause and condition for developing the Bodhi mind.

What is respecting spiritual self-nature?

That is to say that this consciousness of ours today, compared to the consciousness of Shakyamuni Tathagata, is truly no different, no different. Why did the World-Honored One attain Enlightenment early in countless lifetimes, while I am still in a coma and crazy, still an ordinary person? The World-Honored One has countless magical powers, wisdom, and dignified merit, while we only see countless afflictions, karma guiding us, and binding us to life and death? With the same mentality, confusion and confusion are as far apart as the sky. How could it not be shameful to calm down and consider? It's like a priceless pearl lying in the mud, treated like a tile and pebble that no one appreciates.

Therefore, we must use countless good dharmas to treat afflictions, diligently practice morality, then our virtuous nature will be revealed, like that pearl that is washed and polished and hung on a high, brilliant throne, shining and illuminating everywhere. Only then can we say that we do not betray the Buddha's teachings and do not waste our own spiritual enlightenment.

That is the seventh cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is repentance of karma? (duṣkṛta): refers to the group of light sins in the precepts, so it is also called a light sin.

NOTE 2

Each day and night in the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings is equal to 50 years in the human world. Therefore, the time mentioned here is more than 9 million years in the human realm.

but still suffer such karma, let alone serious crimes, the karma is truly hard to describe!

We today, in our daily activities, every action and movement often violates precepts; Every bite of rice and sip of water is always against the rules of etiquette. Countless sins have been committed every day, let alone in a lifetime, over many lifetimes, the sins that arise are certainly indescribable!

Just considering the Five Precepts alone, there are nine transgressors out of ten, but there are few who reveal them, and many who conceal them. The five precepts are only the precepts of lay people but have not yet been fully kept, let alone the novice precepts, monks, and Bodhisattva precepts. Surely the shortcomings are too obvious to need to be said. If someone asks you, you immediately claim the name of a monk, but in reality you have not yet fulfilled the virtues of a lay person. Isn't that shameful?

You should know that the precepts were established by Buddha, it is better not to accept and keep them. Once accepted, you should not break them. Once you break them, you will eventually suffer the fall. If we do not soon develop a heart of compassion for ourselves, compassion for others, pain for others, pain for ourselves, pain in body and speech, pain in our mouths, tears falling with sincerity, for all sentient beings, sadness and repentance, then surely in thousands of lifetimes, it will be difficult to avoid bad retribution.

That is the eighth cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is praying for birth in the Pure Land?

That is to say that in this Saha world, monastic practice

progress is very difficult; If you are reborn in the Western Pure Land, achieving Buddhahood will be easy. Because it is easy, it can be completed in one lifetime, but because it is difficult, many lifetimes remain unfulfilled. Therefore, everyone has looked up to the sages of the past and present; In thousands of sutras and treatises, everywhere points to the Pure Land.

In the age of the end of dharma, there is no dharma that surpasses the Pure Land. However, in the sutras it is taught that only a few good roots cannot be reborn, but only a lot of virtue can be achieved. If you want more blessings, there is nothing better than reciting Buddha's name; If you want to inherit good roots, there is nothing better than developing a broad mind. Therefore, reciting the holy name, even for a moment, is better than someone giving alms for a hundred years; Once you have developed the Bodhi mind, you have overcome many lifetimes of practice.

Reciting Buddha's name has the hope of becoming a Buddha. If you don't develop a great mind, then what is the use of reciting Buddha's name? Developing the mind is to practice. If one is not born in the Pure Land, even if one sets the mind, one will turn back. Therefore, if you sow Bodhi seeds in the field of mind, use a plowshare to recite Buddha's name, then the path and fruition will naturally grow. Relying on the boat of great vows, entering the great sea of ​​Pure Land, the Western world, decided to be reborn.

That is the ninth cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

What is it that makes the Dharma last in the world for a long time?

That is to say what the World-Honored One has done since countless eons until now, for us to practice the Bodhi path, even difficult things can be done

Yes, difficult things can also be endured, until the cause and effect is perfect, finally achieving Buddhahood.

After becoming a Buddha, saving sentient beings everywhere, the causes and conditions have ended and then entering Nirvana. The stages of Dharma and Dharma have all passed, now only the end of Dharma remains. The Dharma is not practiced by anyone, evil cannot be distinguished, right and wrong cannot be clearly known; Everyone competes and follows self, everyone seeks fame and fortune. Looking across the vast world, it is all like that, no one knows who Buddha is, what the Dharma means, what is the name of Sangha? Having degenerated to that point, I can't even bear to say it, every time I think about it I suddenly have to cry.

We are Buddhists but we cannot repay the Buddha's gratitude, we do not benefit ourselves, to the outside world we do not benefit others, living in this world is already useless, dying will not benefit us in the future, the sky is high but cannot protect us, the earth is thick but cannot support us. So, the one who carries the heaviest sin, if not me, then who is it?

Therefore, the pain in my heart is unbearable and I can't think of a way to make it whole. Suddenly he forgot his incompetence and aroused the vast Bodhi mind. Although it is currently impossible to restore the end of life, we will definitely take care of protecting the Dharma in the future. That's why I went with my good friends to the ashram, prepared a repentance dharma, established this dharma assembly, and made 48 great vows, each vow to save sentient beings. May I always keep my mind deep and steadfast for hundreds of thousands of eons, every mind is the Buddha's mind.

From today until the endless future, at the end of this life, I vow to be born in the Pure Land, progress to the ninth level of cultivation, return to the Saha world, make the sun of Buddhism shine as brilliantly as before, the Buddha Dharma will once again expand throughout the world, the Sangha are like a vast ocean of purity in the entire world, everyone will be saved right here. Saha, life is prosperous and virtue increases, Dharma lasts a long time in the world; Such a sincere and earnest wish.

That is the tenth cause and condition to develop Bodhi mind.

The ten causes and conditions as above are all known, the eight tendencies to generate the mind are also clearly understood, so the direction is available, the starting point has been determined. In addition, I have a human body, live in a civilized place, have normal six senses, have a healthy and peaceful body, and have enough faith and faith. Fortunately, the path of practice has no obstacles.

What's more, today we can become monks, receive full ordination, see an ashram, hear Buddha's teachings, admire Buddha's relics, practice repentance, meet good friends, and have all the perfect causes and conditions. If I don't develop the Bodhi mind today, then what day will I wait?

I only hope that the masses will sympathize with my sincerity, even if it is foolish, and feel sorry for my hard-working and persistent aspiration. Please, together, develop the Bodhi mind and establish the Bodhi aspiration. Those who have not yet developed their mind, today should develop their mind; If you have already developed your mind, please increase it; already growing, please continue without interruption. Don't be afraid of difficulties

If the towel is rotten, don't be so easy-going that you take it for granted; Don't be too impatient and not be able to maintain it for a long time; don't be lazy and lethargic but lack courage; Don't be weak and lose your excitement, don't procrastinate and wait uncertainly; Don't give up and not pay attention because you think you're stupid, don't think you can't participate because of your slow nature. For example, when planting a tree, over time the shallow roots gradually deepen; Or like sharpening a knife, if you sharpen it for a long time, the dull blade becomes sharp. Why don't you plant the tree because you see shallow roots and let the tree die? Because you see that the blade is dull, but you don't sharpen it, leaving the knife useless?

Furthermore, if you think that practicing is hard, you really don't know that laziness and indolence will be even more miserable. Cultivation brings temporary hardship, but eternal happiness; laziness brings temporary peace for a lifetime, but suffering for many lifetimes. What's more, if you rely on the Pure Land boat, you don't have to worry about turning back? If you have the Dharma of non-birth as your strength to endure, why should you be afraid of hardship? You should know that there are sinners in hell, and there are also those who have developed Bodhi mind from previous lives, let alone Buddhists in the human world, who do not make great vows in this life?

Because of ignorance and darkness since beginningless time, the events of the past cannot be prevented; If we are awakened today, the future can be changed. Those who are ignorant and unenlightened are inherently pitiful, but those who know but do not act are even more painful and pitiful. Introduction In the Dhammapada Sutra, the Buddha taught that: “Dharma

gift trumps all giving.” Practicing Dharma giving means sharing and spreading Buddha's teachings to everyone. Every Buddhist can, depending on their ability, practice Dharma giving in the following ways:

1. Try to learn, understand and practice the Buddha's teachings. The deeper you learn and understand, the more effective sharing and giving Dharma will be. Remember that reading books is more important than buying books.

2. You must cherish the scriptures and books printed with Buddha's teachings. When you have the means, buy them and bring them home so that you and your family can learn and follow them. You should not keep it as your own, but be willing to share it, spread it widely, and encourage many others to read and learn. You should not let the scriptures lie still and collect dust on the bookshelf, because if the scriptures are not read by people, they cannot bring benefits.

3. Depending on your ability, contribute material and effort to support those who do the work of compiling, translating, printing, and circulating scriptures, so that more and more precious scriptures can be printed and circulated.
